reviews_content: A cozy Korean-style kids café perfect for little ones (0–6 yrs). The space is compact but full of fun zones—mini kitchen, ball pit, dollhouse, wooden cube sandbox, and a baby play area. Parents can relax with coffee or order food (charging spots included) while keeping kids in sight 👀☕🍴  -  Clean, safe, and thoughtfully designed. - Entry fees apply to both kids & adults, playtime is limited to 2 hours, parking is only free for 2 hours with stamp, and it can get crowded during peak hours.  Overall, a charming spot for a quick family outing—just bring socks, plan around the 2-hour play limit, and try weekdays for a calmer vibe 💛 || Mari Go Round Premium Kids Cafe is a nice, relaxed place for kids to play while parents can sit back with some food and drinks. There’s a slide, a bounce area, and plenty of toys to keep little ones entertained. It’s not overly crowded, and the environment feels very kid-friendly, both inside and outside.  We visited around noon, so the toys were already scattered all over the place—but that’s to be expected with active kids. The food isn’t particularly impressive, but it covers all the basics for both kids and adults, and the prices are reasonable.  Overall, a good spot for families looking for a casual play cafe with enough space and variety for children to enjoy themselves. || Tucked away quietly at the back of the Racquet Club residences, this kid cafe offers a cozy and welcoming atmosphere that makes it a pleasant escape for families. The theme is charming and inviting, creating a warm environment for both kids and parents to relax and enjoy.  The entrance fee is quite reasonable: 100 Baht for adults and babies under 12 months, with unlimited stay duration. For children aged 12 months and above, the fee is 250 Baht for a limited two-hour window. I only tried their nuggets and simple drinks, which were okay — nothing extraordinary, but decent enough. I can't comment much on the food since my experience was limited.  One area for improvement would be the cleanliness and tidiness of the space, especially when the place is not busy. It seemed a bit neglected at times, which is a bit disappointing for a kids cafe where hygiene is important. The diaper table is very small from IKEA, and its pretty not up to safety quality for babies at 6 months+ anymore. The bin and overall changing station can be maintain or improve better.  The staff was present at the counter throughout my visit, but I noticed they were mostly occupied with their phones and didn't appear very friendly or attentive. Friendly and engaging staff are essential in a kids cafe, so this was a minor letdown.  On the plus side, the location is convenient and has potential for hosting parties or special events. With some attention to cleanliness and staff friendliness, this place could become a favorite spot for families in the area. || This place is so fun for the kids. It was a nice way to spend time during the rain. I appreciated the offering oh healthy snacks for purchase and the variety of imaginative based play offered. My kids found it very fun and really enjoyed the ball pit and slide the most. || Mari Go Round Premium Kids Cafe is a small but well-designed indoor playground located inside RQ Residence on Sukhumvit 49/9. It’s a cozy spot where parents can comfortably monitor their children while enjoying a small café setup.  Pros:  ✅ Convenient for Parents – The small size makes it easy for parents to keep an eye on their kids while relaxing, eating, or even working. ✅ Decent Play Area – Includes a ball pit, slides, climbing wall, and educational toys, keeping young children entertained. ✅ Café Inside – Offers food and drinks, making it a convenient place for a casual visit.  Cons:  ❌ Limited Parking – Free for only 2 hours, while the minimum play session is 2 hours, meaning most visitors will end up paying an extra 40 THB for parking. ❌ Entry Charge for Everyone – Both parents and children must pay to enter, even if you purchase food. ❌ Small Space – While cozy, it may feel a bit cramped during busy hours. ❌ Shared Parking with Residence – Can be difficult to find a spot, especially on weekends.  A convenient and cozy place for parents who want to relax while their kids play, but the entry fee policy and parking situation make it less appealing for longer visits. This was our second visit to Playmondo, and it’s quickly become one of our favourite indoor play areas in Bangkok. The space is bright, colourful, and full of variety, with zones for climbing, sliding, and jumping. The play equipment suits a range of different ages: my kids are 2, 4 and 10 but we also went when they were 1, 4 and 9 and they all still had many areas they could play in safely.  As a family with autistic children, we really value how open and well-designed the layout is. There are quieter corners where kids can take a break if they feel overwhelmed, and plenty of seating areas for parents to stay close by. The lighting isn’t harsh, and the sound levels are manageable compared to many other indoor playgrounds.  Everything is clean and well maintained, and the staff are often whizzing around cleaning and hoovering to keep it in great condition. It does get busier at peak times, but it still feels safe and welcoming.  There is also a small cafe where you can order simple meals like cheesy fries, ham and cheese toasted sandwiches and many types of drinks.  If you’re travelling in Bangkok with kids — especially if you’re looking for somewhere fun, safe, and sensory-considerate — Playmondo is a great choice. We’ve enjoyed it both times and will definitely be back again.  Unlike the Harborland play places, Playmondo let's children and parents wear any brand of anti-slip socks - so you won't find yourself forking out for even more on the spot. || Thank you for taking the time to review Playmondo! They have a roasting facility in the Sukhumvit area.  Area: I always visit their coffee kiosk at the Silom branch, which is located in a small alley beside the Kamakamet shop.  What’s I ordered: I ordered an Iced Americano with a single specialty "S-31" (Ethiopia Sidamo Bombe G1), which has a slight to medium roast body and acidity. This is my preferred style when ordering an iced Americano. Another recommendation is the Silom Blend, which is great for those who love medium roast with low acidity.  Prices: The prices are acceptable for specialty coffee, starting at 120 THB. They also offer non-coffee beverages for those who cannot drink coffee.  Overall, I think it is the best specialty coffee around Silom and a great option for office staff. || Friendly barista and staff who can recommend and explain details of each beans. We tried b4, my mom love it. We will be back. || Excellent coffee. I'm happy to suggest the B5 coffee bean to anyone who like the aroma of rum in their coffee. || Enjoyed the coffee. Wished the size could be bigger. I finished the cup after afew sips😄 || Nice coffee beans, Orange espresso was superb, recommended!!

place_name: Blue Coffee UC At One Bangkok
reviews_content: Delicious tasty roast coffee. Cute little shop and very friendly staff who's speaking English. I'll be back || The drinks never disappoint! Even though they’re a bit pricey, we keep coming back to Blue Coffee whenever we can find it. This time we ordered Ice Cocoa and Peach Coffee. The Peach Coffee doesn’t beat the Noire, but it’s still good for me. The subtle aroma and the slice of peach really bring out the fruity flavor. I’ll definitely try another drink next time 🫡  I’m giving 4 stars because of a small issue. We ordered the Soft Cocoa and ask without cream, but the first waitress didn’t mention anything. When the order arrived, it was exactly as shown in the photos (with cream). We explained that we didn’t want cream, and another waitress came over to apologize, explaining that the menu is supposed to come with cream. She offered to change the order to Ice Cocoa and refund 10 baht. It was a bit disappointing that the first waitress didn’t mention this upfront. Overall, the drinks are always great 🙌 || Incredible taste of drinks, super coffee  Matcha cream is just 100/100  👽 || Ordered the matcha coconut water and it was delicious ! If you like your matcha taste strong, then this is the drink to order. Very refreshing. 👍😊 || This coffee shop has an amazing atmosphere—cozy, stylish, and perfect for both work and relaxation. The coffee is rich and flavorful, with a great selection of pastries to pair. Friendly baristas and great service make it a spot worth returning to || Quite good coffee, seating area has Japanese vibes (don't know why, as I think they're originally from Chiang Mai) staff though was not very welcoming, it seemed like I interrupted an "important" TikTok session for them, which is of course, always most important in Thailand, than serving the customers who indirectly pays their salary.  So, although coffee was good, I won't come back. I don't want to bother them. Hopefully they will get more free time for TikTok soon. || The queue is a bit long when I was here on a Friday 330pm. There was only 1 staff serving. But I have to say the matcha coconut juice is really tasty. The shop looks so Japanese and it’s easy to find a table. || very good coffee, good place to hangout with friends and family for coffee time, nice ambience & cozy, very good service and friendly staff🥰 i enjoy my time here✨ thank you blue coffee! || Coffee was great, i recommend order 50% sweet as 100% is too sweet. However, staff was moody and the google map said they closed on 22.00, but they close since 20.00. || Good coffee taste with good vibes for awakening mood

Very nice place with excellent coffee. Love the seating area at level 2. Is a great place to chill with friends and enjoy a good cup of coffee. There are parking spaces outside the shop but might be limited especially during peak hours. || Today we dropped by a specialty coffee near by ari station The shop has parking in front of which is easy to park and drop by  The shop style and the baristas looks so cool  Ordered black coffee balanced bean which is middle roast 100baht Es yen dark roast 60baht Dirty set contains matcha chocolate and coffee dirty 250baht Totally 410 baht today Worth to try || I tried many cafes in Bangkok, but this one stands out for me. Every coffee that they prepare is super yummy. The owners are super friendly and love to help you choosing the right coffee. I highly recommend the Dirty coffee here. You will not regret it. || The coolest cafe' in Bangkok that I've visited. 👍 Umeshu was mixed between espresso and salted plum. It was bitter and salty but tasty. 😋 I love it! Another one for my sister  is Cocoa Strawberry 🍓 || Flat white with dark roast coffee beans is quite delicious. I like the classic menu. There are also some signature drinks on the menu.  I enjoyed drinking my coffee on the second floor of the cafe, which is decorated well. There is a big table to work on laptops or study.  I visited the coffee shop again after two years and had a delicious hot latte. || The barista did have a hard time understanding my English but the cappuccino I've had here is prolly the best one I've had (five+ countries I've been to). Loved the ambience here too. || The coffee was very good. Not to miss is their blueberry cheesecake. We ended up ordering an additional slice to get our fill. Just perfect! || I tried 2 cups of latte. 1. MAE JAEM / PAHEE (washed, medium to dark roared) 2. JHOMTHONG / HUAI NAM KHUN (Natural, light to medium roasted) Both were pretty good. I preferred the second cup more since it had nice apricot and tropical flower notes that I like!  ☑️English ☑️Cozy ☑️Nice hospitality ☑️Local Thai coffee  Thank you💕 || Stylish coffee shop in Bangkok, very friendly & authentic staff. The Flat White was very tasty. Many different beans you can choose from. Can highly recommend Black Specialty Coffee! || a good ambience, with a wide variety of coffee beans. Overall, a memorable coffee experience

It’s the perfect place to recharge and grab some specialty coffee after eating and shopping at Chatuchak.  The owner is super friendly and shared her knowledge. We also brought home some grains to make our coffee at home, with amazing smell and taste. Definitely a happy reminder of our time in Thailand. || Excellent cups of speciality coffee. We loved the arabica beans from Nan, Thailand that is yeast fermented. The geisha Ethiopia and Panema beans were also excellent. Definitely should ask for hand poured coffee so you can taste the beans, adding milk to such good coffee would be such a waste! || Definitely a must-try shop if you are a coffee lover.  Before deciding on my coffee, the owner let me smell different beans—like ones processed with a whiskey method, with rose aroma, natural process, and the shop’s signature beans from Chiang Mai. For the first time, I noticed a subtle durian note blending into the coffee beans.  In the end, I chose beans from a Thai origin for a hand-brew. The drink came with the owner’s creative touch! It was decorated with cinnamon and rosemary, which added more layers to the aroma and flavor.  The first sip had a rose note (though maybe because many drinks pair rose with lychee, I always get the illusion of tasting a sweet lychee flavor XD). After holding it in my mouth for a moment, the rosemary gradually emerged.  I didn’t expect the owner to be collaborating with Da Vinci Coffee for COE—it turned out to be a surprisingly nostalgic coffee experience for me XDDDD || This place was absolutely amazing! She takes coffee and makes it a whole new experience 🙌 I’m so happy that we stopped by and met the owner, Lara! She treated us with such fantastic hospitality. My husband had the whiskey coffee, and I had the one with the chocolate notes. || Fate brought me to this cafe!  Visited second time because I was drawn to specialty brews as well as to the kind and friendly owner! I can see that each coffee is made with love and care. Enjoy the music and love to talk to the owner.  It’s a shame that I live far away, but I’ll visit the café whenever I come to Chaktuchak market. || The weekend market has a real pearl for specialty coffee fans. They make fantastic coffee cocktails. The lady owner is a real coffee fan, who runs her cafe with a lot of heart and love🤗. For real coffee lovers, it is a must to visit and taste the seasonal offer. I also recommend it to anyone who is just starting to learn about coffee because they can get useful information. There are wonderful blends in the world of coffees and fruits. Absolute top place! || Such a hidden gem away from the hustle and bustle. Place was air conditioned with nice music and ample seats. Most impt, part timer rouny was really patient and knowledgeable of the coffee. She allowed us to smell the various beans before deciding and offered us kombucha and coffee extract samples. Thai nan beans were really fragrant with whiskey notes while their speciality blend was interesting with durian notes. Fully recommended! || One of the rare finds i have at chatuchak 😊 owner Linda is very knowledgable and she is passionate in her coffee. Ask her about her special beans and recommendations, she will be friendly and happy to share with you! || Must try if you are a coffee lover. Tried one of their whisky fermentation beans and very pleased! || Best specialty coffee cafe in JJ market and perhaps even Bangkok! Walk pass the cafe and it has seat with aircon. The cafe offers variety specialty beans for selection esp the Thai specialty beans. I tried Columbia cold drip coffee, it comes in very fancy serving and the owner also let us try the special Oolong cold brew with Grape scent, very refreshing.  The shop also sells specialty coffee beans. Must visit place when coming to JJ market.

A good place to have good coffee with a twist, we order a factory white and a white Citrus; both taste great. The place is large with positive feel, clean and tidy. Best of all at, it is situated at the end of the airport rail. Highly recommend . || i ordered the salted egg croissant, mrs. cold, and supreme. everything was really good, especially the drinks! the milk in both drinks was super creamy and just delicious  the salted egg croissant was okay when i ate it later, but i’m definitely coming back to try the fresh baked ones.  it’s a unique flavor for sure though! definitely a cool spot to check out for great coffee and creamy drinks. Kudos to the cashier, he was really nice & helpful || I finally caught The Coffee Factory open after a previous missed visit, and I'm glad I did! I tried their signature "Moscow" coffee, which had a unique and refreshing flavor profile—even if it wasn't my all-time favorite. The real standout was the Thai tea-filled croissant: an unexpected and delightful twist that made for a fun, flavorful snack. Overall, my visit was more about enjoying the cozy vibe and trying something different than chasing perfection. If you're in the mood for creative drinks and treats in a welcoming atmosphere, The Coffee Factory is definitely worth a stop! || Visited for a caffeine break. The queue was at least 30 minutes so I thought why not go all out and make it worth the wait by ordering 3 signature drinks. My favourite was Phayathai, refreshing with a unique aftertaste that even non-coffee drinkers like me can enjoy, followed by Mrs Cold, suitable for most coffee drinkers as recommended by the staff, and then Moscow served in a skull-shaped glass, easy to drink but too creamy for my taste. We also grabbed 6 bottles of cold brew thanks to their buy 5 get 1 free promotion. The space is industrial and spacious, making it a nice spot to slow down. || Stopped by Factory BKK for coffee and pastries and it was such a pleasant break. The croissants were beautifully made, flaky and buttery, with unique flavors that really stood out. Loved the charcoal croissant, rich and not too heavy.  The coffee was just as good, smooth with lovely latte art and well balanced flavors.  Everything was nicely presented and the atmosphere was cozy and relaxed, perfect for a slow coffee moment. Definitely a spot I’d come back to. || Tried their Moscow coffee and it was great - the thick layer of milk added much body and flavour to the aromatic coffee - I really liked it.  We also ordered 2 types of croissants - lava chocolate and salted egg - which was so-so, and a little underwhelming given their price tags.  Atmosphere-wise the place had an clean, almost industrial-like vibe to it. But I enjoyed the bright lit and spacious feel overall. || Factory Coffee is one of my all-time favorite cafés — and it’s easy to see why it’s award-winning.  Despite the long queues, it is absolutely worth the wait. Every cup is carefully crafted with excellent balance, depth, and consistency. You can truly taste the passion and expertise behind the coffee.  For true coffee lovers, Factory Coffee deserves both the recognition and the wait ☕✨ || I ordered a Panama Gesha and felt that the brewing method used was not the best choice for this coffee. The cup had quite a lot of sediment and lacked the clarity and delicacy one would expect from a coffee of this price and quality.  On the other hand, the staff was always very kind, warm, and professional. 😁 || Is a great place to try. Afterall BKK is also another coffee heaven for coffee drinkers.  Many different kinds of coffee. Today I tried the white citrus. The coffee was has a strong aroma and the citrus came after that. Is taste a little bitter but overall the drink is tasty.  A hint of sweetness and bitterness after taste. Interesting  The early grey was their signature. And it was only 730 am and only left 5 pieces. The cake has a very strong early grey smell which I love it. The cream on top was not too oily and just turn right amount. The cake is on the drier version. Not the usual fluffy and light kind. Which is why is a smaller peices. Is packed with omph and you can literally taste every early grey in every grain of the cake. Would love to try their carrot cake the next round.  Many people are ordering their IG drink such a supreme coffee as the staff will come over and pour for you to take video and this resulted in long queues. So do be mindful when trying out this place and plan your time well. When I left at 8am. There was already a queue despite it was not seated fully as they need to make sure they can fulfilled all their drinks first. It took about 15 mins for my drink to arrive. So dont expect Starbucks service..and I didn't give 5 stars because once it get crowded. The queues is horrendous.  The design of the cafe is like all other major coffee shop.  Rustic warehouse design with concrete slabs. But they do have nice cute chairs and tables. || Specially went down to this cafe because of tik tok and youtube recommendation. But sadly, the coffee is overrated. The cafe opens at 8am and when I reached at 7.30am, there is a reasonable amount of people queuing to enter. Queued about 45min and ordered 02 cups of 9oz factory white (not latte) and 1 slice of lemon cake. The cake was a surprise. Soft and creamy. But the coffee was disappointing because it is too milky. Barely tasted the caffeine. A cup of white is the basic to me and it wasn't done properly. There is a different between a white and latte. And yet, it cannot be done properly. I guess most of the patrons visited this cafe is to try out their best seller - Supreme.  So if you have extra time to spare and nowhere to go and feel like queuing up, you can try this cafe. Otherwise, do consider other cafes in BKK which at least can do a better white.

reviews_content: We had an incredible experience exploring Old Bangkok with Jobe! He led our group of seven adults with absolute care—always at the front keeping us safe while another staff member stayed at the back to make sure no one was left behind. We bonded with everyone in the group as we biked through alleys, got real glimpses of local life, and stopped to learn about temples, traditions, markets, feed fish, and all the little details that make Bangkok so special. We tasted amazing authentic Thai food and drinks along the way, and one of the highlights was getting nine bikes loaded onto a long boat so we could cruise down the river to lunch—such a fun and unforgettable moment! Jobe captured fantastic photos and even a video of us riding, which made the day even more memorable. He truly made this a 5-star experience. Highly, highly recommend! || We went on a tour with Jobe. He is superfriendly and the pace of the tour is great! Spent the day biking around old and new areas of Bangkok, seeing lots of temples and cultural areas! We had plenty of breaks on the way and stopped to eat some delicious Thai food! A must do if you’re in the area! 10/10 experience!!! || very enjoyable, our tour guide Toni was very friendly and very helpful, you should try it when you go to bangkok thailand. YOU SHOULD ONLY BOOK WITH MANDY TO TOUR BANGKOK!!! she is the best guide!!! || Thank you very much Darryl for your kind review and photos. reviews_content: Tucked away from the chaos of Bangkok’s streets, the Museum of Bangkok is a refreshing step back in time. Walking through the exhibits feels like peeling back layers of the city’s story, from its early days to the vibrant metropolis it is today. The displays are easy to follow, thoughtfully curated, and give real context to how locals lived, worked, and adapted as the city grew. It’s a great break from temples and markets, especially if you enjoy understanding the why behind a place. Calm, informative, and surprisingly engaging—well worth adding to your Bangkok itinerary. || The Bangkok National Museum is a peaceful and culturally important place to visit, especially if you want to learn more about Thailand’s history, traditional art, and royal heritage. The museum complex is spacious, the buildings themselves are beautiful, and the exhibits give you a nice overview of Thai culture, religion, and past civilizations. It’s a quiet break from Bangkok’s chaos and a good spot for anyone who enjoys museums.  However, it’s worth mentioning that the collection is not as rich or extensive as you might expect from a “national museum.” Some sections feel a bit limited, and a few areas could use more modern presentation or detailed explanations. If you’ve visited larger national museums around the world, this one may feel more modest in comparison. || First the shortcomings. The Museum  is not for person with disabilities, even a senior citizen has to careful while climbing 2nd floor.Many floor tiles are uneven. There are no indicators regarding Exit. I got lost and spent 10 minutes to exit. Only room numbers are mentioned. Finally lighting was so poor that it was not possible to read the information cards. Now the positive side many clean hygienic  toilets well maintained. The the collection from earlier empires well documented both in Thai and English. Number of school children were seeing   the collection. Lots of people were taking interest, reading the notes and photography  the works. Different period works were duly arranged and important information  about them provided. Works from Srilanka, India (Pala, Gupta and Sarnatha Mathura period), Java, Afghanistan, Indonesia,Laos, Khmer, Vazrayana (Chines influence) were well depicted. Two cafeteria one which serves Thai cuisine and the coffee shop next to ticket office. There is a well stocked artistic works in Museum souvenir shop. Some renovation is ongoing so not all could be accessed. But thanks for such rich Thai heritage in which my country India,  Buddhist and Hindu philosophy and religion  have kindred contribution. Buddha Namah! || An iconic tourist attraction in Bangkok and also one of the most beautiful places I’ve seen in Thailand. Put on nice socks because you will have to take your shoes off to enter some rooms like in many places in Thailand. As it is a very touristic place, unless you go first thing in the morning, it will be crowded so don’t expect to take pictures with nobody in them. Also bring a bottle of water because the place is huge. However the architecture with so many different styles is very impressive and the atmosphere amazing. The collection of artwork is impressive and you can learn a lot about the history of the country. So beautiful. I highly recommend || Lovely museum with loads of great exhibits. I would recommend to focus on buildings 4 and 5 (the ones at the far end of the compound) since those provide a comprehensive overview of local history history, starting at prehistoric times and ending in the 19th/20th century. The exhibits' arrangement might seem a bit dated, but the nice and tranquil atmosphere even on an otherwise busy Friday afternoon makes up for that. || Please be advised, video recording not encouraged. 240baht for foreigner. Flow is great, we went in the order of 1, 4 (golden boy), 5 and finally 6. Buddhism artifacts from various countries. Art styles from Lanna to recent Rattanakosin. Spent around 3hours or so. Making of Mother of pearl, Bencharong ware etc. Worth the visit. || Good attraction to spend at least half a day if not more. Well laid out museum and not too busy. Extensive history of the nation well documented and explained with many interesting artefacts. Cafe serving Thai food and refreshments situated about half way round and a coffee shop next to the ticket office. Unfortunately, some renovation work being done on my visit but didn’t impact too much. || Tons to see, lots of history to experience and learn about. There are several buildings to explore that cover different periods in history. Some sections require you to remove your shoes. Remember to sheets be respectful and not too loud.  There's a cafe inside with not great food or drinks but it'll do the job if you're hungry.  Some of the buildings are more modern and have elevators but some of the buildings are older and would be harder for wheelchair users ♿️ || Historic art is exhibited at this museum. Very rare items of Thai history & culture. Lot of information on each art piece. I learn a lot about my own country here. Very beautifully displayed. || It's a really big museum with a lot to see, so be sure to plan plenty of time for visiting it. It's great to see it during mid day, when the sun is high and it gets too hot for comfort to walk outside. The entrance has a free baggage room, to make the visit to the musuem more enjoyable.

First time visitors from any country should visit the Rattanakosin Exhibition Hall as a starter. Not as large as the Bangkok National museum this exhibition hall gives you a basis for thai culture. The 2 hour tour is recommended as they go through the timeline of the country, the king lineage and architectural development. Also, there are evolutions of the long boats which were interesting to me. Lots of knowledgeable facts throughout the 4 floors and a overlooking floor to see the temple on the top floor good for photos and videos. No flash however in the main building. Highly recommended! || So much fun and the staffs take very good care of us. Very impressed. Good exhibition || Truly the best ever experience to fully understand the Thai culture and history. Spent total 4 hours with a guided tour just for 100baht admission fee. Tour guide speak fluent english they even prepared a guided tour machine with super clear explanation.  If you’re interested in Thai history, cultural, Royal family. This is definitely the place to visit! Highly recommended to finish the whole 4 hours tour. The guided tour that i joined starts on 1pm sharp and 2nd tour is at 3pm. Not sure on the exact schedule. || Free entrance during certain holidays. We took route 1 that covers the history side and although it was interesting, we wish they could shorten route 1 duration and offer both route 1 & 2. English guide is available, staff is polite, clean facilities. || I took route 1 and it helped me understand the history of Thailand. It was an interesting experience and worth a visit. || Great place to learn about Thai history and culture under the influence of the current monarchy. The entry fees are absolutely fair considering the input you get by these exhibitions, made with love for details. || Excellent place to learn more about Thailand's history, culture, Thai people and also to have a great, enjoyable time. The entry fees are 70 Bhatt for the locals, 100 Bhatt for the forginers and free for any one over 60 years old. The exhibition provides a free official guide to visitors and translation. The staff are very proffisonal, friendly and helpful, providing the visitors with excllent service. || What a great experience to know about the history of Thailand and Bangkok. There are 2 routes for you to choose to learn about. It takes approximately 2 hours which is worth! If you have sometime in Bangkok, definitely check it out! || This was very very good.  There are two paths to the tour.  We took the path that has the simulated boat ride because the path with the rooms had one room under renovation. We went during the week, and since there were no other visitors at that time (hint for others), we were treated like vip guests.  The tour was great, we could take our time, we could sit in the auditorium style settings anywhere we wanted, the tour guides were quite helpful and answered our questions--even took pictures of us with the props at the exhibition hall. At the end, going to the top and looking out over the city, we had a great view of a couple temples--Golden Mount & forgot the other one, where we took pictures and rested for like another hour.  It was a fabulous view on a great day. I would recommend it for anyone especially during the week.  ( it was 100 baht/person). Also, in December they are planning night at the museum style exhibition around the middle of the month, sounds interesting. || A very impressive introduction to Thai Culture, tradition and history. There are two types of guided visits, both are recommended. It takes almost four hours to go through the complete place. Language translation is available through the use of wireless radio sets. Use of animations, videos and sound effects is simple amazing, it makes the whole experience worth it. In fact through use of visual aids they have expertly made the history lessons so interesting and easy to remember. A must see for someone who is interested in the history of Thailand. Few things have been left out keeping in view the laws of govt / monarchy

I spent about two really nice hours here. The house is beautiful, and the lush garden a calm, shady place.  I joined an English-speaking guided tour, which was easy to follow and very informative. In about 40 minutes, the guide gave us all a great overview and shared interesting background about the place.  I also had plenty of time to walk around the garden and explore a few of the other buildings on my own, both before and after the tour.  There’s a shop with lovely silk items, though many are on the expensive side. The restaurant is a nice extra and a good spot to take a break during your visit. || Jim Thompson House Museum is one of the most fascinating and rewarding cultural experiences in Bangkok. Tucked away in a surprisingly quiet and green area of the city, the museum offers a sharp contrast to the surrounding urban energy. From the moment you enter, you feel transported into a different time and atmosphere, calm, elegant, and deeply rooted in Thai culture. The traditional teak houses are beautifully preserved and thoughtfully arranged, showcasing an impressive collection of Asian art, antiques, and architectural details. Every room tells a story, not only about Thai craftsmanship and aesthetics, but also about Jim Thompson himself, his vision, his passion for art, and the mystery surrounding his life. The guided tour is highly recommended. Informative, well structured, and engaging, it adds real depth and context to what you are seeing, turning the visit into a meaningful cultural journey rather than a simple walk-through. The gardens are equally charming, lush, peaceful, and perfectly integrated into the experience, making the visit feel relaxed and immersive. Overall, the Jim Thompson House Museum is a must-visit for anyone interested in Thai history, architecture, and culture. Elegant, authentic, and thoughtfully curated, it offers a rare glimpse into a refined side of Bangkok that is both inspiring and memorable. || Quite an interesting place. TBH, I wasn’t planning on visiting the Jim Thompson House Museum; however a friend had programmed it into our itinerary. The guided tour of the house was very interesting, and the design and structure of the house (which contains pieces assembled from six other houses) was very impressive. Also the artefacts contained within were simply stunning. It appears that Jim Thompson and his incredible work to promote Thai silk worldwide left an indelible mark on Thailand. || The restaurant at The Jim Thompson House is truly exceptional — a perfect blend of elegance, Thai charm, and warm hospitality. After exploring the historic teak houses and beautiful gardens, dining here feels like the perfect continuation of the experience.  The atmosphere is refined yet relaxing, with thoughtful design touches that make the space feel both sophisticated and inviting. The food is beautifully presented, full of authentic Thai flavors, and the drinks — especially the cocktails — are outstanding.  What really elevates the experience is the service. Gam, Fon, and Arm were absolutely wonderful: friendly, attentive, and genuinely welcoming. They made the entire visit feel personal and memorable.  Whether you’re visiting the museum or simply looking for a classy spot to enjoy Thai cuisine, this restaurant is a true Bangkok gem. Highly recommended! || Spent a lovely hour and a half here. Easy to get to via the canal taxi boats. Beautiful house and lush garden. Cool on a hot afternoon. Bags go in a free locker before tour starts. Shoes on for part of tour and off for the house. We went on one of the English speaking tours. Our guide was clear and informative. It took 45 minutes in which she gave a good overview. We had time to take photos in each space. We then spent another 30+ minutes exploring the garden and a couple of buildings on our own after the tour. There is a shop with beautiful silk products, but most things a bit out of our price range! We popped into the Art Exhibition too. A lovely way to spend an afternoon. . || We thoroughly enjoyed our visit to the Jim Thompson House. Please be advised that you can enter the house only as part of a tour. English lead tours should be around every half an hour and last the same time. Our tour guide was amazing. She was very knowledgeable and witty. Not only was she able to answer any questions she also provided some memorable puns with professional delivery. 🙏🙏🙏 We also enjoyed visiting the shop and would have loved to buy more since the prices are less than half compared to European outlets. || I was surprised just how interesting the tour was - they managed to fit a lot into 45 minutes without it ever feeling rushed. The focus was equal parts Jim Thompson's life story and the history of Thai culture and architecture. Would recommend booking ahead. || The Jim Thompson House is an absolute must-visit in Bangkok — especially for anyone who loves design, architecture, or history. Every corner is visually stunning, from the beautifully preserved traditional Thai teak houses to the lush tropical gardens that surround them.  The restaurant and café are also wonderful — elegant, relaxing, and a perfect spot to unwind after touring the house. The food and drinks are excellent, with the same thoughtful design touches that make the entire experience feel special.  A true Bangkok gem that blends art, culture, and craftsmanship. Highly recommend! || Interesting man and a nice museum if you are into interiors and architecture. The arts centre next door is a very interesting design. It is quite hot, so dress appropriately. The tour is included in the entry fee and was well coordinated and interesting. || I visited the museum in 2019 and fell in love with this hidden treasure in the heart of Bangkok. I visited again to see this place again and I was still amazed at how beautiful and peaceful this place is. I would definitely recommend the visit, and I would personally go with the flow in terms of tour times. It’s a place where you can sit and relax until your tour time. It’s been 7 years since I’ve been and I’ll definitely visit again on my next trip to Bangkok.

Walking distance from Watmankong Kamalawat, this community unit aims to restore old buildings around their neighbourhood. It’s crazy imagining once people really lived there. Chinese assimilation in Thai’s society went really smooth that the nation only identified as Thai. No wonder the country is generally safe, prosperous, and able to offer such kindness and sincerity. My huge respect for Thailand as a country, a nation and Charoen Chai private funded museum for initiating such a gift to the world 🙏 || Nothing much except some old stuff. The area is tuck away at an alley and you just go up the stairs, you will see all in 30secs. Not even well kept. || Enter Soi Charoen Krung 21, walk past the market, turn right. Not far from Wat Mangkon is a very small museum. It was originally a residential house to show the way of life of the people in this area. **Charoen Chai community area, so it was made into a museum. There is no admission fee, you can take pictures. || This museum is located up some stairs inside an old building.  The place is very small and there's not much to see, although admission is free and it's worth visiting if you're in the area. || Follow the map and when you reach the entrance, you will be a little confused because this building is located in the middle of a shop that still has people living there. When you walk up the wooden stairs, you will find a small museum that is well-organized and tells the story of the building and its objects. It is like hearing old Chinese music floating by. || The "Old House Tells Stories" museum is located not far from Wat Leng Noei Yi, in Soi Charoen Chai 2. It's a two-story commercial building over 100 years old, with a rather steep staircase leading up. The museum houses a collection of artifacts from the Chinese community that once lived there. It showcases ancient history and culture, some of which still survive, while others have faded over time. The museum's current condition is rather dated, but that's understandable, as it was probably created by the owner's descendants, who wanted to tell the story and likely didn't receive any support. || A museum that tells the story of the lifestyle of the Chinese community and the beliefs surrounding paper offerings in Charoen Krung.  Free admission.  Donations are welcome to support the cause. Inside, antiques are displayed, and the history of the Charoen Krung area is narrated. This particular house was actually the residence of people in the past. || Very impressive. The house of someone who actually lived there. The upper floor is decorated with old collectibles and things that remind me of the atmosphere where someone actually lived. The walls are still in their original color, with some peeling paint showing through. The windows and doors have anti-theft metal. The inside is not stuffy as I thought because the thick cement walls keep the house cool. But I'm secretly haunted by the dolls in the storage room.

Golden Teak Museum has an admission fee of 30 baht per person. The amazing thing about this place is the wood that was used to build the entire building. One can attempt to justify how solid the teak wood is by going to any of the pillars and have a tap on it. It’s simply dense!  I was told that the outer pillars which are painted white in colour are actually teak wood as well. After having known this fact, I took a second look and it really looked like a concrete pillar and amazingly strong on par.  At the second level, there are many 1-1 size of famous monks made in wax. The resemblance is fantastic. (Refer to panoramic photo). The eyesight of each wax statue is uncanny true to life. It’s as if each statue is alive and looking at you.  In different corners of the building, you can see photos and books of great history. It is definitely a place that tourist or even locals should visit at least once in their life. || Worth to visit if you’re in the area. Best example of teak wood at its finest. Thai culture and history of all the past Buddhist Chief Abbots on display and much more. Recommended! || Intresting spot. Might be boring to some but I liked it. House made from teakwood including all furniture. I loved the photographs everywhere, they really tell a story.     It's located inside the     area.   Ticket 30baht.   Worth a look if you visit the temple || Had a pleasant experience visiting the museum and was accompanied with a lovely lady that, albeit minor language differences, gave me a thorough presentation of the history of teak wood as well as the other exhibits. If you are in the area I’d recommend a short visit to the museum. || There are friendly staff members to explain things when you visit the Teak Museum. || The Golden Teak Museum, located in Bangkok, is a unique and fascinating destination dedicated to showcasing the beauty and historical significance of teak wood in Thai culture and architecture. This museum offers visitors an immersive experience into the world of teak craftsmanship and the rich heritage associated with this valuable material.  Architectural Marvel: The museum itself is housed in a striking building constructed predominantly from teak wood. This structure exemplifies traditional Thai architecture and craftsmanship, making it an architectural marvel in its own right. The use of golden teak not only highlights the material's natural beauty but also enhances the overall aesthetic appeal of the museum.  Exhibits and Collections: The Golden Teak Museum boasts a diverse range of exhibits that explore the history and uses of teak wood. The displays include detailed information about the processing and application of teak in traditional Thai construction, as well as its cultural significance. Visitors can view beautifully crafted wooden artifacts, antique furniture, and architectural elements that illustrate the versatility and elegance of teak.  Cultural and Historical Insights: One of the key attractions of the museum is its focus on the cultural and historical aspects of teak wood. The museum provides educational content about the role of teak in Thai society, including its use in constructing traditional buildings and its economic importance. This educational aspect adds depth to the visitor experience, offering a greater appreciation for the material and its role in Thai heritage.  Visitor Experience: The museum is well-maintained, with informative displays and friendly staff who are knowledgeable about teak wood and its significance. The peaceful and aesthetically pleasing environment of the museum complements the exhibits, creating a comfortable and engaging experience for visitors.  Overall Impression: The Golden Teak Museum is a unique and enriching destination for those interested in Thai culture, architecture, and craftsmanship. Its combination of beautiful teak architecture, informative exhibits, and cultural insights provides a valuable and memorable experience. Whether you are a history enthusiast, an architecture aficionado, or simply curious about Thai heritage, the Golden Teak Museum offers a rewarding and educational visit. || Nice photos inside, but I didn't find the visit interesting || It is the nation treasury which must visit! All the collections value could not quantify in numbers. Thanks to the owner, they do the right thing for country. || Very friendly staff, beautiful wooden museum and wax figures of important monks. Recommended! || If you have the chance, please come visit again. Thank you very much. || I couldn't see it inside but looks like a very interesting place to visit.

Sai Suddha Nobhadol Building is an architectural and historical landmark in Bangkok. This charming palatial mansion, formerly the home of a royal spouse, is now part of a respected university.  The mansion offers a unique perspective on Bangkok's architectural and historical landscape. Its elegant design, historical significance, and serene surroundings provide an enjoyable and meaningful experience for those interested in Thai architecture and heritage.  It is highly recommended for both locals and foreigners, and it is free. || Absolutely charming palatial mansion, built as residence of one of royal spouses, currently belongs to the respected university and houses extensive museum exhibition along with tradirional and high Thai cooking demonstration class and display. Truly amazing place, with gigabytes of history carefully preserved in hundreds of original material exhibits, paintings and photographs. || Unfortunately, we arrived close to closing time and couldn’t fully enjoy the entire exhibition. However, it was a very enriching experience. This house belonged to a noble lady around 100 years ago and has been transformed into a museum with beautifully restored interiors that retain their historical value.  The museum is located on a university campus, and the surrounding area is lovely for a walk. It was a fascinating visit, and we’ll definitely return to explore more. || Sai Suddha Nobhadol Building, located in Bangkok, is a notable landmark known for its historical and architectural significance. As part of the broader heritage and cultural landscape of the city, this building offers visitors a glimpse into Thailand’s rich architectural history and royal heritage.  The Sai Suddha Nobhadol Building is renowned for its elegant design and historical context. It reflects a blend of traditional Thai architectural elements with influences from other styles, creating a distinctive and aesthetically pleasing structure. The building’s intricate details and craftsmanship showcase the artistic and architectural skills of the period in which it was constructed.  One of the key features of the Sai Suddha Nobhadol Building is its historical importance. The building has been associated with significant historical events and figures, contributing to its cultural and historical value. Visitors interested in Thai history and architecture will find the building’s background and design particularly intriguing.  The surrounding area of the Sai Suddha Nobhadol Building adds to its appeal, with well-maintained grounds and thoughtful landscaping enhancing the overall experience. The building’s location within a broader historical and cultural context provides additional opportunities for exploration and learning.  While the Sai Suddha Nobhadol Building may not be as widely known as some other landmarks in Bangkok, it offers a valuable and enriching experience for those interested in exploring the city’s architectural heritage. Its blend of historical significance and architectural beauty makes it a worthwhile visit for anyone looking to delve deeper into Thailand’s cultural history.  Overall, Sai Suddha Nobhadol Building is a hidden gem that offers a unique perspective on Bangkok’s architectural and historical landscape. Its elegant design, historical importance, and serene surroundings make it a meaningful and enjoyable destination for visitors interested in Thai heritage and architecture. || The tour guide explained that King Rama V commissioned this palace to be built as a home for Her Royal Highness Princess Maha Chakri Sirindhorn in case of a future change of government. He also named the palace in memory of Her Royal Highness Princess Maha Chakri Sirindhorn.  Visiting this place and imagining the lives of people in the past was truly impressive. One curious thing about the secret staircase was the smell of fragrant flowers wafting up to your nose. 😊  After admiring the palace, it's a short walk to the Kaew Chao Chom Restaurant. The food is delicious, with a moderate flavor and a warm atmosphere. They offer a menu of rare, traditional dishes. I highly recommend it. 👍 || 📍: Sai Sutthanaphol Building Museum  This museum, housed in the old royal residence in Suan Sunantha, is very old and beautiful. 👍🏻  #1stEyeView || Architecture that still exists and can be learned at Suan Sunandha Rajabhat University. || If you love old-world atmosphere, Thai-style furniture, and nostalgic memories, you won't be disappointed here.

I’m not sure why there were some negative reviews about this coworking space, but I really enjoyed it. Everything was very clean and tidy. There’s a nice café inside with tasty and varied coffee options. The receptionist was super friendly and welcoming. The space itself is large, comfortable, and on a Friday it wasn’t crowded || Hi Alexa, we are pleased you had a positive experience with us and thank you for taking the time to leave us a 5-star review score. We hope to see you again soon! || The best co-working office space in Bangkok! Spaces is more than just many offices in central Bangkok of various shapes and sizes with fantastic views from the 24th floor and brand new, attractive furnishings plus a clean, spacious cafe, enormous reception/common areas, meetings rooms, etc. It is the Spaces team who deserve a special mention...everyone at the Reception Desk, behind the counter in the cafe, the cleaning staff and the management (who are always close by and available) are more than friendly and helpful! They make Spaces the great working environment it is!! || Nice place for working,  meeting and study. Location is in center of Bangkok , can go by mrt or bus. They are very good decorations as co-working space should be,  comfy chair and table,  have enough space for each groups,  use earth tone that make people feel  relax. They also have mini meeting rooms and private room for only 1people! And the view is very cool,  you can get the light from outside,  not only from neon , coz there are many big windows along a wall || Very spacious and nicely decorated. Good atmosphere. Not being overdramatic, I gave two stars thanks to the woman in the front desk who yelled at me for the very first impression; she needs heavy training on how to be service mind if she wants to still be in this business. Whenever I walk, she would stare at my like if I was going to steal her things. Casa Lapin coffee is reasonable price. || Great and convenience location. Great view toward Chulalongkorn University. Nice furniture set and decoration. || Great Coworking offices, ideal for events, centrally located || The location is great! It offers a lovely view and is located centrally right next to Samyan MRT station. I genuinely love spaces and frequently use the one in my hometown Zurich, Switzerland as well as others when I am travelling for business. Unfortunately, this one does not yet live up to the high standards set by the other branches. The gentleman at the reception is as unwelcoming as they come and highly demotivated and answers questions only reluctantly.  Unfortunately, in an estimated 80% of spots there is no possibility for charging your electronic devices so you will have to recharge your device while taking breaks. This does not help productivity. Generally the facilities are not up to date as the toilets lack cleanliness and are sometimes malfunctioning. In two of the toilets was no paper The wifi speed is simply inadequate, nothing more to say about that.  The little café is lovely and the service very friendly. The venue has a lot of potential which is currently not used to the maximum.  I hope my review will be taken to heart and the next time I visit I will find an inviting atmosphere that will enable me to concentrate and work efficiently. || Nice location, if you can live with slow internet and janky toilets.  Location is quite nice, just a few more steps from MRT Sam Yan station, the overall facility is considerably good.  For months, the staff could not mitigate the internet issues (low bandwidth and high latency). Moreover, they promised to improved but it's never been delivered.  Toilet could be a problem especially for the ladies. Since they could not afford more cleaners to do their job frequently, expect the filth lying around the restrooms. || Does not allow walk-ins, members only. Can work for 2 hours from the café with a purchase of a drink, but no wifi. || Hi Olga, thank you for your feedback. Memberships are available from 5, 10 or unlimited days a month with no booking required on the day. You can also book day offices or meeting rooms. For further information please head to spacesworks.com/products-services/ or contact our sales team. Thanks. || Greatest co-working space ever

Quite a high quality office with reasonable rent for anyone who wants to start own business.  Good for company image.  Professional service! || Best service office ever || My office is here, love it. || The recent earthquake prevented access to the office and damaged it. However, the tenants were allowed to return to work despite the unsafe conditions. They continued to collect the full rent, but were unable to contact any employees. || Hi Elle, Thank you for sharing your concerns. We are very sorry to hear about your experience following the recent earthquake and understand how worrying such events can be. Please be assured that the safety of our tenants is our top priority. Following the earthquake, inspections were carried out both inside your office and throughout the building. We can confirm that your specific office has not sustained any damage and is still fully operational. Additionally, the building has been assessed and certified as structurally safe for use. Thank you. || Please avoid Regus and IWGPLC in Thailand. They are the biggest scams. Once you sign a lease with them they have a lot of hidden costs that you can't imagine. They also charge customers for printer and WiFi connectivity. You can't downgrade your contract once you sign it. You will have to pay the full rent for the signed contract even if you want to leave. This office service is the biggest piece of crap ever. Please avoid this modern day scam. || Hi Kerrisdale Travel, we're sorry to hear about your frustration. We'd be happy to help but were unable to identify your account based on the information you provided. Please contact your center team so they can assist you, or you can log in to your ticket through the help section of your online account. Thank you. || One of the most complete and modern serviced offices, suitable for professional companies or organizations. Impressed with the service. || Online store open all the time || Hi Shingaek, thank you so much for taking the time to leave us a review. We'd love to hear more about your experience with us. We hope you'll visit us again soon.

place_name: JustCo – Samyan Mitrtown | Coworking & Office Space
reviews_content: Stunning co-work with panoramic views across Bangkok. The space is beautifully designed, with various private and group areas for collaboration centred around a nice coffee roasters. The reception/experience staff Kan, Kate, Bo, Mamaew, Ju were extremely friendly and provided a 5* welcome. Very impressed!  The only downside is that there isn't a coffee machine here, just the cafe (around 60 THB for a coffee) and instant sachets. Not a problem if you have cash or Prompt Pay. || We truly appreciate your positive review, Daniel! It’s wonderful to know that our space is meeting your expectations. Your happiness is our motivation, and it’s fantastic to hear that we’re on track to being the ideal place for you. Your feedback means a lot to us, and we’re excited to continue offering a space that caters to your needs. Thank you for being such an important part of our community. || I’ve been working from JustCo Samyan Mitrtown for a while now, as our organization just took a dedicated space here, and the experience has been nothing short of amazing. The space is clean, modern, and perfect for productivity but what really makes it stand out is the incredible team running the place.  Kan, Bo, Kate, and MM are genuinely some of the friendliest and most helpful staff I’ve ever met. They always greet you with a smile, assist you quickly whenever you need something, and create such a welcoming atmosphere that it feels more like a community than just a workspace. Whether it’s helping with meeting rooms, handling small issues, or just brightening your day with their positive energy, they truly go above and beyond.  Highly recommend JustCo Samyan Mitrtown not just for the workspace, but for the wonderful people who make it special. || Thanks so much for the great review Khun Sushil! We’re delighted to hear that the space meets your expectations. Your feedback truly means a lot to us, and we’re glad to know we’re on the right track. We appreciate having you as part of our community. || Very well-managed coworking space and easy to reach by MRT. The place has multiple floors, and the rooms are spacious enough to fit larger groups of around 30 people. Reception is on the 24th floor, and the staff are professional, friendly, and always helpful. They gave a clear tour on the first day and continued to support us with small requests and questions. The central aircon can feel a bit too cold at times, and meeting rooms are available at an additional cost. Overall, a comfortable and convenient workspace that I’m happy to recommend. || Thank you for your review Khun Sutawee! Your feedback is invaluable and truly appreciated. It’s wonderful to know that our space is meeting your expectations. Your happiness is our motivation, and it’s fantastic to hear that we’re on track to being the ideal place for you. || Super comfy workspace with great lighting, tons of room, and a spectacular view, honestly hard not to enjoy working here. reviews_content: Amazing atmosphere and great service. The jazz music and cozy decor make it the perfect spot to unwind. Huge wine list and tasty food. Located on the 2nd floor of One Oasis. Definitely coming back!🍷 || What an absolute gem! I stopped in by myself and was blown away by this cozy wine bar. So many places like this treat food as secondary, but here it's clear they put immense care into their menu.  ​I ordered two dishes, and it was the perfect amount for a satisfying solo meal. Both were exceptional: ​Grilled Cauliflower Steak: This was perfection. The cauliflower had a beautiful char that gave it a crispy exterior while remaining soft inside. The sauce elevated the entire dish. I'm still thinking about it and would happily return just for this "salad"! ​Spicy Crispy Pork Pasta: A really interesting and bold dish. It had a wonderful, authentic Thai-style heat and was packed with flavor. The crispy pork was a great touch.  ​As for the wine, the selection looked impressive, but I'm no expert, so I'll leave that for others to judge. For me, it's the outstanding food that makes this place a must-visit. Highly, highly recommended! || A nice place for Wine Lovers near All Seasons Place  I recently visited this tucked-away wine bar near All Seasons Place, and it was such a pleasant surprise.  Right from the start, I was impressed by the staff. They are polite, well-trained, and genuinely service-minded. They were not only attentive but also very knowledgeable about both wine and food, offering helpful recommendations throughout my visit.  I ordered two dishes: 1. Burrata & Grilled Orange 2. Classic Carbonara  The Burrata was fresh and slightly cream. It's exactly how I like it. It paired perfectly with sweet grilled oranges, juicy tomatoes, a hint of bitter rocket salad, and savory ham. Personally, I’m not a big fan of vegetables, but the rocket’s bitterness wasn’t overpowering, and I still managed to enjoy the whole dish.  The Classic Carbonara was rich and comforting. What stood out the most for me was the crispy, flavorful guanciale, absolutely delicious! They mentioned the Carbonara is made in the traditional style, though I’m not a huge Carbonara fan, so I can’t compare deeply. I originally wanted to try the Real Truffle Cream Pasta, but unfortunately, it was unavailable that day, so Carbonara became my backup choice.  Travel Tip: This wine bar is located in a small Soi, and honestly, the entrance might surprise you. It’s not the kind of place you’d expect to hide such a charming bar. After walking past All Seasons Place, keep an eye out for a small alley with a discreet sign overhead. Once you spot it, turn left into what feels like a flea market-style lane. The bar is tucked away on the second floor of the building on your left.  If you're driving, you can park at All Seasons Place and bring your parking ticket for the restaurant to stamp. However, be aware that the surrounding roads often suffer from heavy traffic, especially during after-work hours. Taking the BTS and walking might be a faster and less stressful option.  If you're looking for a relaxed yet refined wine and dine experience in the city, this place  should be on your list. I’ll definitely return, hopefully next time they’ll have the truffle pasta ready! 😁 || Thank you so much for visiting us, we are looking forward to serve your again. 🍷🙏🍾🎷 … || Real hidden gem in the area. That wasn't even a problem until one staff, a big tall guy coming at us speak so poorly without any service mind like we bothering him.
