Such a poorly service mind staff totally ruined the experience and shouldn't work in customer service. The other guy (smaller and younger one) was a lot better and even apologized on his behalf. What a shame to have a junior apologise on your behalf. || It’s so fun the lane was very professional and I would like you guys to try it out 20 out of 20 experience ❤️ || Bowling here was a whole vibe — the good kind! Came with a group and had a blast. Definitely a step up from your average bowling alley. And you know it’s legit when the DJ is dropping their own tracks. || Good bowling alley in Bangkok, nice DJ, attentive staff, and reasonable price. Honestly, they need to do full maintenance on the pin machine since it was stuck many times.

Monday and Tuesday promotion, 3 games 150 baht. Regular price 70 baht a game. I showed up at about 4 o'clock and it was packed with teams. Only a few lanes were available. The place starts to clear out around 18:00. A jug of beer was 200 baht. The balls were a bit beat up and the heaviest one I could find was a twelve. I played 6 games and had a great time. The staff were great! || This place is almost perfect in terms of the quality of the lane and atmosphere. But, FYI, I would have given five stars if there weren’t occasionally some employees who didn’t seem so friendly and welcoming—just a few of them. Overall, this place is fantastic! I've been bowling here for months now. They do have a pro shop, too! And the products are crazy good imported stuff from the U.S.  The guy (Beer) in the pro shop is a great guy! Highly recommend him! It takes him less than an hour to drill you a ball.  The prices are so reasonable, too!  Three games for 210.- Bath from Thu-Mon Three games for 150.- Bath on Tue-Wed +Shoes rental for 40.- per pair (if needed)  Btw, they have a special price for ladies on a particular day, too! Three games for 120.-  Oil pattern: Kegel (Wall Street 7240) 40ft || Took my daughter bowling today and she had the best time! The place was super cool.the restrooms were clean, and the staff were all so sweet and helpful. Such a fun day! || Great place, cheap and very good lanes. || Great activity for family and friend. Price is very comfortable. We are so happy. || Bowling place for sport. No loud EDM music like other commercial place. Cheap local and clean. There is shop selling bowling equipment. You can order food and drink there.  Promotion 3 game 150thb + 40thb for shoe renting. || Bowling center is old, lanes are refurbished and staff was excellent,  The lighting in there could  be better and just an FYI the Bowling center is upstairs. || Nice place to go bowling. Games are cheap. Not as fancy as some other places in BKK but has everything you need. Staff were friendly and they have competitions. || Not flashy or modern. But awesome for people that enjoy bowling. It's quiet and super cheap (2 games for 100baht). Staff were nice and pleasant.  Lanes were good, balls were fine.  It's a little out of the way though. || Hidden gem bowling in Bangkok City 🥰🙏 …

Bowling and ice skating side by side. This is a great family outing if you want to avoid the scorching heat from outside. Bring your kids for lessons or open skate. Great location attached to the mall. || To be fair, not quite a full 4 ⭐, the essentials are there though, good service, clean and well maintained. Not the latest and greatest but definitely ok. Around 190 a game, but they often have some kind of promotions, so do check.  F&B is good (once their kitchen open fully after Covid19) 👍 || Great place to take small children bowling. Wouldn’t recommend for competitive bowlers as balls get stuck often and mis-drops on pin resets are common occurrences.  Sure, I can give you a random bowling alley review!  This bowling alley has a fun and relaxed atmosphere with friendly staff members who are always ready to help. The lanes are well-maintained with modern scoring systems that make keeping track of your score easy and stress-free. They also have a great selection of food and drinks that are perfect for snacking on between games. Overall, this place is a great choice for a night out with friends or family! || Applied for student membership to get better rate, membership fee is 50 baht which I think it worth it. Kids enjoyed very much. Good service as well. || All of us had a great time. The system is well maintained. The service staff are friendly and helpful. They don't allow outside food and drinks. Understandable || We had the private room and it was a lot of fun! It was well worth the price and great service. I would go back again for another party. However I hope they improve their food menu and repair their bathrooms. || Even more fun to be here with friends! There's also food and drink for you to order with a fair price (may even be lower than outside). They got their mechanic team standby behind the bowling mechanism all the time, and their waiter/waitress are very helpful! || A great place to bowl, all the lanes seem to work well and plenty of different size bowls to suit each player. The staff are very helpful and amenities are very clean. || Used to be a great place. On a Saturday afternoon the music is way too loud. Food is not great. Tables are not cleared right away leaving plates and glasses from those who were there before we arrived. || Very nice bowling area. You can eat as well and the food was very nice. We took pizza, fruits, fish and other... Dessert nice as well. As far as the bowling is concerned they have a lot of aisles to play and they provide some aid for the little kids also. They have around 20 aisles but there is a lot of people waiting. In weekends you should prepare yourself to be on a queue. We had a birthday party there and they provided some stuff like alcohol shots and candles and a big board saying "happy birthday" etc... they had a promotion that if you spend at least 4000 baht you get a small blanket.

Bowling and karaoke. The place was very well maintained and specious. Variety of foods and drinks (coffees, soda and alcoholic drinks) for a great price. They also has private bowling party room for a group of family or friends. || We had a great time there. We went there as a big group with 7 kids. The staff were very nice and helpful. We brought a cake to celebrate BD of our kids. To our surprise, when we brought the cake, the staff started  playing the HBD song and even brought a big backdrop and a HBD light up sign for us right away. We were very impressed because we did’t expect any of that. The kids had a lot of fun and we all had a wonderful time. 😍 || Back here after so so long, almost 8 yrs! Not much has changed around here. Bowling alley , shoes, and ball/bowls were well maintained. Staff were really polite, helpful and friendly. Service was top notch too. Food though is another question. To save the day.. get a bucket of Popcorn from Major Cineplex right next to it! Overall, it was a fun vibe and still a great idea for a get-together. || Tunes were good,  nice place. Works out around 10bt a ball/bowl || Well maintained lanes and bowling balls. Good food served at your table and friendly staff. My family had a lovely time there and the price was reasonable. Special prices offered by the hour. || Birthday celebrations are good theme for private groups and reasonable || Very nice bowling alleys. Doesn't lack at anything. Nice alleys, big variety of balls, very delicious food (Khao pat gung was extremely delicious), drinks... || Bowling is good but need alot of improvement regarding food, chef should always taste the food cook if is tasty people would stay longer but if food is no good people would only come for games. I didnt give 5stars cause of food need to be better. || Beautiful place for bowling One of my favorite place for fun with kids

Great service and amazing atmosphere. Play pool while you wait for your lane, beers and a DJ. Good times. || Great friendly service. Pretty affordable to play a quick game. 220thb per person per game, 50thb for shoe rental, 60thb for socks. I wish there was by the hour option. The ball racks aren't really organized too well but then again this isn't a place for serious bowlers. It's not for the younger crowd to hang out. || Good place, good vibe! They have carousel of sweet colorful shots, super fun!! The only thing is, the holes in balls are too small for a European gal. || Went on a relatively quiet weekday night for Karaoke. The experience was relatively disappointing. The initial room we had issues and the staff had to move us to another room, eating into our time. The room was quite comfortable and relatively average with what you'd expect.  Unfortunately, for the price, it wasn't worth it. The staff were nowhere to be found and the call button was about to fall off the wall. We had to walk all the way to the bowling bar before we found staff members to order. Everything else was average, what you'd normally expect from Blu-O. Nothing exceptional though. || This is probably the best bowling alley in the whole world. It's super fun and they sometimes have live bands and  the food is delicious and they serve great beer. You can get the beer in towers with ice, which is awesome. The bowling experience is great. It's a perfect place for a fun party with a group of friends. They also have private karaoke booths in the back, which are also very fun. I highly recommend this place. || It was a fun place especially you were with your friends. || Great place to bowl with your friends 🎳 Not very crowded as Siam Paragon and plenty of cheap food options and beers to select. They got some deals as well, where you play 2 hours, unlimited games.  Balls are bit smaller though, so if your fingers are big, you will find it a bit difficult to handle the smaller weights. But an overall fun filled place. Definitely recommend you to try as well. || Came here for two bowling games. Staff took us very quickly, within 10 minutes we were playing. Cannot complain, the price was 190 per game per person, 50 for shoes and 50 for socks. || Great atmosphere..good bowling . Great times. || I had a great time here.  The bowling was a little expensive but the employees were very nice and accommodating.  190 baht per game, shoes = 50 baht or 1000 baht per hour.  I'll go again.

This is the place you can spend your time with full enjoyment .come and take experience.good place for visit .and parking is free of cost . || Lots of lane, lots of staff, service good and fast. Equipment is new. || Terrible place. The DJ starts shouting at everyone while you’re trying to bowl and won’t shut up. He keeps going. It’s super loud and you can’t bowl a frame.  For this price I don’t want to be shouted at. ฿1100 for 2 people 3 games.  Never seen it in my life. Don’t bowl here. It’s fun until the DJ starts going on and on over the loudspeakers, then is straight sucks. It’s super loud honestly. || We went bowling here and karaoke. Bar available and food || Terrible customer service, cheated || When with my son who was visiting us from UK || This is a really big bowling alley. It's a complete facility with a restaurant, karaoke, and VIP rooms, perfect for families and groups of friends. It's especially suitable for large groups. The prices are quite reasonable per game. || The area is a good size, with 20 regular lanes, karaoke rooms and VIP lanes. The staff are friendly, the equipment and area look clean, the atmosphere is good, and the music is fun. || The staff are very helpful. There is a bowling shop where you can throw bowls and a karaoke room where you can sing. If you are a student, the price is good. I recommend coming with friends. It is very fun. If you come on your birthday, try asking about it. There might be a promotion where you can play bowling for free after you have finished playing. It is a game. || Bowling lanes, the screens are quite old, the DJ only plays slow Thai songs, listening to them doesn't feel fun, so I don't feel like staying long.

Fantastic place to learn about the history of Bang Rak and Thailand in general. The museum consists of three beautiful houses set in a peaceful garden, each showcasing different aspects of traditional Bangkokian life in the mid-20th century.  The keepers at each house are incredibly kind and welcoming. They go out of their way to explain the background of each building and the history of the items on display.  The site features three beautifully preserved houses. One highlights the lifestyle of the original family, while others include interesting exhibits like a former medical practice and historical items from the World War II era.  Entry is free, though it is highly advisable to leave a donation to help with the maintenance and preservation of these heritage buildings. || This is a great little place to travel back in time for a moment. The house itself is beautiful and remarkably well-preserved for a home built almost 100 years ago, filled with many artifacts from the era. I especially loved the volunteer 'aunties' who went out of their way to teach us about the house and the family's history. The whole tour only took about 25 minutes and it was completely free, which is an amazing act of kindness from the family to open their home to the public. Highly recommended! || It's really worth coming here to visit, to take a look at how people lived in the early 1900s in Bangkok. It's nice to take a walk in the house and feel what it's like, and it items in the house have been maintained as they were. It's free to visit this museum and it's currently being maintained by the government. || I loved the visit to this house. Entrance is free. Quite oasi in the middle of chaos. 😅 Everything is well preserved. The descriptions are not well written and sometimes difficult to understand. I didn’t like the fact that the stuff was taking pictures and maybe video of me and other visitors without asking for permission. || It's free. It's something to do. A family home where the father was a doctor and some connection with royalty. From the World War II era through the 70s. The staff are nice. They'll take photos of you while you browse. || Staffed by volunteers, free entry. Very beautiful gardens and three houses to check out. The third one is air-conditioned, so if you need a break, that is a great place to stop.  If you like museums and enjoy seeing technology, history, architectural history, and how life used to be, it is a great place to visit.  If you are middle-aged like me, you will probably see a lot of things that are close to your childhood, from your childhood, or at least the predecessor of something you grew up with.  Really glad I walked here. || A cool museum free of charge allows you to see how Thai people used to live. There is air con in one of the buildings. Beware of the wooden stairs as they may get slippery. || You probably get a good insight of how the good old days in Bangkok was then, looking at the exhibits here. Well maintained and kept. Friendly and welcoming staff. || We had read about this museum and planned to visit but the day we chose turned out to be Chulalongkorn Day and AI was telling us it would be closed. Lucky that we ignored AI and still went there because not only was it open but it was free and lovely volunteer staff took time to show us around and explain things. Museum is made up of 3 old houses and they contain a lot of furniture, photos and household items relating to the former owners. A fascinating insight into life in Bangkok for middle - upper class people last century. || This remarkable "hidden gem" survives Bangkok rapid development, with an unassuming nature that the public mighg pass through without noticing it. The best part is that is FREE!!! There are three buildings in the yard- the resident bungalow, a clinic, and a "bachelor" house which are todays gallery with relics of the past. You will be accompanied by the staff who not only acts as guide but also to ensure the safety of the exhibits and visitors.

You will discover beautiful art spread across six floors of this museum. It is recommended to allocate at least two hours to fully enjoy your visit. The museum features intriguing paintings and sculptures created by Thai artists. After exploring, consider visiting the café.  The best way to reach the museum is by using Grab. There is also a designated area to store your belongings if needed, and they accept credit card payments. || I visited MOCA Bangkok on a weekday and had a really great experience. There was no waiting time at all, which made the visit even more enjoyable. The entrance fee was around 300 baht (if I remember correctly), and it was definitely worth it.  The collection is impressive — a wonderful mix of contemporary Thai and international artworks. I could take my time and really enjoy every piece. The museum itself is very comfortable, clean, and well-designed. There are plenty of chairs around, so if you get tired walking through the galleries, you can easily sit down and rest for a while.  There’s also a museum store where you can buy some nice merchandise and souvenirs, and a café where you can relax and enjoy a cup of coffee after exploring.  Overall, it’s a great place to spend a few quiet hours appreciating art. Highly recommended if you’re in Bangkok and love modern art! || Located a bit north from downtown Bangkok, however this is still very convenient to get to through Grab or Bolt. Apart from the evergreen art display, installations with the current exhibition GOLDEN TEARDROP are gorgeous! What's more is staffs here are super helpful to make your trip a very delightful experience :) || The museum is worth the visit and i have no idea why I kept putting it off for so long. It is a 5 floor building with a great design. The works of art are worth contemplation and it is very easy to navigate the exhibitions. There was no wait but there were other guests. There are lifts and escalators which means anybody with limited ability can enjoy the museum. Toilets are available at each floor. You get to learn about Thai artists and appreciate their artistic paths. The tickets as advertised cost 300 or 150 if discounts are applied. Payments made in cash or by card. No food or drinks are allowed as mentioned on the website. Bags are left in the deposit. The staff were kind and informative. Overall, a great visit and you will enjoy it if you would like to learn about Asian art. If you have any questions, check the museums FAQ section before coming. Ps. Some reviewers miss the point. One mentioned staff were rude and only smiling people should be employed. With that logic, perhaps Thailand should only allow tourists who are courteous, kind, polite… and obviously fast 😉. Enjoy your visit. || Experience of a life time. Such an incredible collection of Thai and international art. Felt so special to be summered in the Thai culture. Last time here was more than 10 years ago, so happy to be back again. Worth every moment. || The most beautiful museum in Bangkok. Visited on Friday and was not crowded before 2pm. It's near the immigration office (Lak Si station) so it's a perfect day trip to this area if you need a visa extension and quiet time for art. || What a marvelous museum. Nice and serene environment, well lit art work and of course the art itself. You can easily spend multiple hours here. Just go and enjoy. || One of the best surprises in Bangkok. The building itself is beautiful and full of light, and the collection gives a great overview of modern and contemporary Thai art – from huge, detailed paintings to sculptures and more experimental pieces. You can easily spend a few hours here wandering through the floors without feeling rushed or crowded.  What I really liked is how calm and well organised everything is. The spaces are quiet, air-conditioned and very well maintained, with clear signage and friendly staff. It’s a perfect break from the chaos of the city and a must-visit if you’re even slightly interested in art or design. Totally worth the trip and the ticket price. || Amazing gallery with fabulous art. Super clean and great choice of contemporary art! Impressive and must visit while in Bangkok || Amazing museum worth every penny. Can easily spend all day here, lots to see across many floors. Nice cafe too drinks are reasonably priced. We used Bolt taxi to get there, short wait finding a driver to bring us back during peak times.

Extremely impressive complex of several specialized museums, including four (general medicine, pathology, forensic, parasitology) in that very same location. Very informative, bilingual, however, I don't think general visitors should find its display interesting and appealing, as some parts of it may look pretty shocking to those far from medicine, forensic or crime investigation.  Photography is strictly prohibited inside museums. My photos shown here were made from museum entrances. || A little hard to review this place. It’s very informative but you need a strong stomach to go here. There is actually 3 museum and they cost 100 baht each. Free for Thai. All three museums have some interesting stuff but lots of dead bodies and babies in jars. So if you don’t mind seeing that this place is for you. It also has a bit of a hospital smell. I’ve added some pictures of the exhibit that are appropriate but not of the dead bodies inside, just be warned! Some pictures are of the other two museums, my favorite was the boat museum which has the largest wooden boat ever found underground and also no dead bodies at the boat museum || If you have a lot of time in Bangkok and you like museums, the make sure to visit this museum. You can buy 1 ticket that covers 3 buildings. Even though I am not that much interested in the medical stuff, I still found this place interesting and worth it. || Fantastic Museum of Anatomy, Pathology,  Parasites, Medical Museum.  This museum let's you get a real life up close view of real bodies and all parts inside of bodies, great selection variety of specimens, curated in a very respectful way in a medical facility.  Definitely worth a visit, to see, up close how we all are made.  Amazing 💛 || Nice place to visit for doable price if you're interested in anatomy and the hunan body. I do think it's quite a shame that for the medical museum part most description are only in Thai. || A definite stop for those that have any interest in this amazing place. I thoroughly enjoyed my time from start to finish. Top notch educational experience for anyone interested in medicine, anatomy, forensics, or just the macabre  The exhibits are deeply informative, a bit intense, and seriously one-of-a-kind. It’s not your average museum and that’s the point. You’re getting honest displays of the human body and medical history. If you have a weak stomach, find someplace else for your sensitive nature.  As for the 1-star reviews? Ignore them. They’re clearly from people who either didn’t understand the complex or probably shouldn’t have visited a museum like this in the first place.  Only thing of note that can be taken negatively is the lack of AC, but they have open windows and fans blowing, so if you can handle that, this is an amazing stop to add to your itinerary! Take my advice, don’t miss this if you’re nearby and have the time to do it! || My friend had a medical appointment at the hospital, so I decided to visit the museum while waiting for him. Paid 200 Baht which gave me access to all three (maybe it’s a special thing during COVID-19), and I spent two hours visiting everything. I enjoyed all the display of anatomical, forensic, cultural, and historical perspectives. || Siriraj Medical Museum is definitely one of the top museum in Thailand. If not, one of the best in South East Asia. Whether you are here for academic research or just to wonder around to kill off some time.  The easiest way to reach here is via ferry (siriraj pier), opposite to tha prachan pier.  As many google reviewer says, although it is quite an adventure but surely is not for the faint of heart. Please do eat before you visit the space, and definitely not for children under 15 yrs old.  There are 3 museums split inside. Dont worry, the counter receptionist will guide you with a leaflet (Eng Language as well) and there are English signage from one museum to another as well.  Photos are not allowed except for the Siriraj Bimuksthan Museum and the pre historic building where you can get to know more during the area within WWII.  Medical students, there should cover you many aspects of medical care, theory and researches purpose. But for quite - squeamish person like myself, I still do enjoy it, but it is very disturbing when seeing corpses and trauma injuries (homicide, suicide etc) graphic visuals.  There is some audio tech to assist you for Non-Thai speakers. Not too sure about "request touring" for Eng language. Would be great to have one at an additional cost. When I was there, I only witnessed Thai Speaking small group tour/walk through.  Ticket Prices for Local: 80 THB Ticket Prices for Foreigners: 250 THB  This is an international level museum. Truly remarkable. Worth the visit. Highly Recommend.  Do check their facebook page a day before you pay a visit. Incase they, closed for covid19 pandemic etc. || This museum is not for the faint of heart, many graphic images of victims, live specimens as well as crime evidence.  200baht per person if you're a tourist. Can be purchased at the museum itself.  There are 2 buildings for the medical/pathology museum. There's also a history museum nearby for an additional 100baht.  Very interesting and educational experience overall.  All the explanations were mostly in Thai language as well as some in English.  (No photos allowed inside) || Quite the experience seeing all the bodies with your own eyes rather than virtually through pictures or youtube. Would’ve given 5 stars if there were more English labels. 300baht for each museum (medical/historical).  Definitely a place to visit when in Bangkok.

Impressive hall, with shoes and drinks at the door policy. Strictly no flash photography or touching anything either!  A shrine erected in the middle of the hall with some antique cabinets at the far end. The craftsmanship and detail is impressive to say the least. Also part of the larger National Museum. || Excellent palace with very impressive murals. The lacquer cabinets at the back are beautiful as well. || See them, cherish them, value them. That is how we learn to realise and respect our heritage, art and culture, the national treasures that reflect Thai qualities. || Visit during water festival in Thailand. Exotic Thai craftsmanship  shown on the wall painting. || Powerful good energy from this Wat || For those in Bangkok, I recommend visiting the National Museum Bangkok to pay homage to Phra Phuttha Sihing, the sacred Buddha image of the Boworn Sathan Mongkol Palace (Front Palace), along with nine other ancient auspicious Buddha images. These Buddha images were graciously gifted to the National Museum Bangkok by King Prajadhipok on December 17, 1926, on the occasion of the Royal Academy of Thailand's renovation and expansion of the museum's exhibition area, celebrating its 100th anniversary in 2026. The event runs until Sunday, January 4, 2026, from 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM.

Now this was an unexpected find for us. We came here as part of a car tour after visiting The Ancient City and I am so happy. The grounds are absolutely beautiful and there are beautiful sculptures, buildings, artifacts, and greenery all around. There is a huge three headed elephant sculpture that sits on top of the largest building and it is pretty surreal to see in person. I could not keep my eyes off of it.  Now for my standard comments. Location is well maintained. Plenty of room to navigate through the smaller crowds during the time we were there. || Visiting The Erawan Museum in Samut Prakan felt like stepping into a magical fusion of art, history, and spirituality all wrapped inside a gigantic three-headed elephant. From the moment I saw the towering statue from afar, I was struck by the sheer scale and intricate artistry. Up close, every detail sparkled—the glass mosaics catching the sunlight in dazzling patterns that seemed almost alive. Inside, the experience was surprisingly intimate and contemplative. The museum is designed with three symbolic floors that tell a story of the universe according to Thai lore. Walking through, I could feel a real sense of reverence and calm, especially in the upper floors housed inside the elephant’s heads where gilded relics and sacred artifacts are displayed. The craftmanship here is unlike anything I’ve seen—each corner filled with vibrant colors and intricate designs that invite you to slow down and appreciate the devotion behind the work. What I loved most was how the museum combines a cultural lesson with a sensory experience—you hear the subtle sounds of bells, see golden statues bathed in natural light, and even get a glimpse of the founder’s vision in preserving Thai heritage. Yes, some parts were warm and less ventilated, but that just made it feel more authentic, like stepping into another era. The grounds themselves are peaceful, perfect for a slow walk after taking in all the art inside. I also appreciated the practicalities: signs in English that explain the symbolism, and a small café nearby to reflect on the visit. If you are interested in something deeply Thai, beyond the usual tourist spots, The Erawan Museum is worth a half-day trip. I left feeling both awestruck and grounded, carrying a richer understanding of Thai myths and artistry, wrapped in one unforgettable experience. It’s not just a museum; it’s a story told through stone, glass, and spirit that lingers with you long after visiting. If you appreciate cultural beauty and spiritual depth, add this to your itinerary. It’s a rare gem that feels genuinely heartfelt and inspiring. || We really enjoyed our visit to the Erawan Museum. The three-headed elephant looks spectacular in real life, much more impressive than in photos. Both the interior and exterior are beautiful, with a lot of detail and a very calm atmosphere. We bought combined tickets for Erawan Museum and Ancient City through the Klook app, as it was more cost-effective. It was a great way to plan a full day, visiting both places at our own pace. Definitely worth visiting. || Erawan Museum is a very spiritual and peaceful place. The atmosphere feels calm and sacred, perfect for reflection and appreciating Thai culture and beliefs.  The architecture is beautiful and meaningful. A great place to visit if you’re looking for a spiritual experience in Bangkok. || Clean and well maintained. The presentation of the very interesting information is not overwhelming so you’ll be interested to read them. It as not too crowded when we visited so we could afford to have a leisurely walk. People working at the museum are all friendly and helpful if asked for any assistance. || It was an absolutely mesmerizing place, located very close to the hotel we stayed at. Although it is slightly outside the city center, getting there by metro is incredibly easy and convenient. There was no need to wait in line at all, which made the visit even more pleasant. I can honestly say it is one of my favorite temples in Bangkok. Taking the time to read the information inside about the temple’s history and learning about its past truly enriches the experience and makes the visit much more enjoyable. And of course, remember that this is an active place of worship, so please be respectful, follow the rules, and be mindful not to overlook them. || 📚 Just visited this gem of a museum and I'm totally blown away! 🌟 Super peaceful and beautiful, especially if you go early before it gets too sunny. ☀️Just a heads up, there are stairs in the inside pink building with the Giant 3 head elephant structure, so not ideal for anyone with mobility issues 🙅‍♂️. But totally worth it for the history buffs - got to see some rad earthenware and ancient jewelry 💎! Would recommend getting there early to soak it all in 😊. || A less popular tourist spot in Bangkok because it is a little further away from all the usual spots. But it's still a marvel of architecture. A brilliant museum that you can spend atleast half a day. Recommended to head there after lunch to avoid the heat and apparently the sunset is stunning. The gardens outside is just as magnificent as the three headed elephant. The middle floor had a lot of mythology that you can spend an hour or more reading if you're a mythology nerd. Thank goodness it's not as popular as the grand palace because it was a beautiful visit. The heat made the outside exploration more difficult but still worth it. || The place is clean, well-kept, the museum itself not big and not very interesting unless you have specific goals to pray which provided outside the museum, but still in the proximity (cause I saw quite many devoted pilgrimage here). You can get beautiful pictures here. The museum divided into 3 section, accessible by stairs (there's lift but only to go up, not down .. maybe for elderly/handicap visitor must request staff to operate the lift for going up & down, but no one near the lift to ask for). Plenty of toilet and clean. There's cafe and air-conditioned rest area here as well. The museum provide shuttle (tuk-tuk) to nearest BTS station with THB20/PAX but do not operate when it is raining. || A super special place to visit. Make sure to visit all floors. The “basement” area has interesting archeological artifacts and a model of a special temple. The grounds are gorgeously landscaped with sculptures, water features, and interesting plantings. My favorite sight so far is

place_name: Tilleke Gibbins Museum of Counterfeit Goods
reviews_content: The staff organized a viewing for us late notice and the museum was fantastic. Sarisa, who gave us a tour was fantastic and answered all of our questions. Highly recommended! || I was welcomed by Ms. Waralee. She explained many things about intellectual property & counterfeiting very well.  Overall, this museum is nice to visit. || Very cool for anyone interested in IP law and copyrights.  Museum only open to the public twice a week but they will accommodate visits out of that time if you give them enough notice.  Museum is run by the law firm and tour is by an associate at the firm. || Sarisa showed us around the exhibit and was able to share a lot of interesting general and legal information about counterfeit goods || We registered a few days in advance via email. The teacher can speak both Thai and English well ;) || Have fun with Christmas party at Saute Dance Studio, such a wonderful extracurricular experience! || Gorgeous school. The teachers are very nice and sweet. They offer various activities from festive to occasional workshops. 10/10 would recommend. 🤍 … || Very nice school for ballet. My kid loves it. || Great Atmosphere with well-skilled teachers. || This academy is a REAL DEAL!!!  Taught by passionate, professional and supportive teachers. They provide our girls with quality teaching where skills and techniques are crucial part of the class.  Set high standards and given every girls their best opportunities to develop their techniques. Love that they are eager to share their knowledge.  It is very warm welcoming and felt like home environment. Plus, Clean, carrying and friendly atmosphere with a safe place.  Last but not least, my 3 girls are really enjoy various performance activities and many festive workshops.  I highly recommend sending your children here!!! || Perfect ballet studio for girls and also family❤️ || Good school to start ballet and enjoyable classes || Very good ballet school for kiddies! || Best dance school in Bangkok.
Brilliant dance school! Teachers are equipped with both skills and experiences. The school offers class for both adult and kid. || great school. higly recommended for both kids and adutls!

Very disappointed with the child safety at this school. A staff member removed my daughter’s sweater and applied hair product without my permission, even when she told them she felt cold. This raises serious concerns about child protection and respecting boundaries.  We’ve been with them for over two years, but recently they kept pushing exam fees and even used the children for promotion during their Open Day without proper consent. This is unacceptable.  We withdrew immediately. Not recommended. || Thank you for sharing your feedback. We are sorry to hear that you felt uncomfortable, and we take all concerns regarding children very seriously.  We would like to clarify some points mentioned in your review:  • At no point was a child’s sweater removed against her wishes. During the examination rehearsal, students are required to wear the official uniform so that the examination number can be properly attached. This requirement is clearly stated in our examination and rehearsal policy, which is shared with all parents in advance.  • Ballet training requires proper uniform, hair styling, and presentation as part of the discipline and curriculum. On that day, some students arrived with untidy hair, and our teacher assisted in making a ballet bun to ensure consistency and safety during class. We had previously shared instructional videos with parents on how to prepare ballet hair before class.  • Parent observation of student progress is part of our curriculum, intended to involve parents in the learning process—not to take advantage of students in any way.  • Regarding Open class activities, participation follows school guidelines and is part of our educational and community programs. We regret if there was any misunderstanding and are always open to direct discussion to clarify concerns.  We truly value the trust families place in us and encourage parents to speak with us directly so we can address concerns promptly and transparently. Our priority has always been the wellbeing, safety, and development of every child. Best regards. Cala Dance Studio || It seems like a good facility. But there are no one-day classes.🥲 …

As an adult ballet learner in 30s who has been dancing here for 2.5 years now, this school makes me love ballet more and more. Teachers here are experienced, inspiring, and very supportive. They not only provide dance knowledge but also healthy techniques so that students can avoid injuries and gain health and mental benefits. My classmates here are also friendly and passionate about dancing so that our classes are enjoyable and effective. Highly recommended for ballet lovers of all ages! - JJ || Thank you for your review. We miss you. 🩰😊💜 … || My kid has a nice progress on her ballet skills from here. At the beginning she does not know much about the ballet but now she really love in love with it and always counting on the class day to learn and practice here. Very recommended for the parent who want your child to love the ballet. || Thank you for your ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ and a wonderful review ka😊 … || Nice school with very caring teachers. Good place to start ballet class. || Thank you for your ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ and a wonderful review 🥰 … || A nice, clean studio with very kind teachers! || Thank you with LOVE💜✨ … || Best dance school 💃 … || Thank you for your review 😊 … || Thank you with LOVE 💜✨ … || This is where I first encountered ballet. Usually, they ask for a trial fee, but this place was so kind that they let me participate in a one-and-a-half-hour class for free. The academy is very clean and tidy, and it's easy to find a watch. The parking lot is also very spacious and plentiful. I recommend it to anyone who wants to learn ballet. 👍💕🙏😊 || Thank you for your review 😊 We are very pleased to have you joined us. 🩰💜 … || The school is clean, the rooms are spacious, and there are many different classes. All ages can learn, from children to adults. The teachers are kind, lovely, and all are excellent teachers. There are Ballet, Jazz dance, Yoga, Thai dance, Modern Dance, and many more. ❤️❤️❤️ I personally come to study both Ballet and Modern Dance. There are also food shops downstairs to choose from and a cafe to sit in. It's very convenient. 💜💜💜💜 || Thank for your ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ and a wonderful review 💜✨ … || The room is very clean. It's convenient to travel. There's a bathroom on the same floor. There are a lot of study equipment. || Thank you for the 5 ⭐️✨ Your feedback is a great encouragement for us 💜 … || Thank you for your ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️💜😊 …

place_name: Dance Centre School of Performing Arts
reviews_content: If you’re looking for a warm, welcoming dance studio that offers high-quality ballet and dance classes for children and teens, this is the place to go. Run by one of Thailand’s top ballet dancers, it’s a fantastic choice. Highly recommended! || Thank you for your review. || Very friendly and competent teachers. || Everything is awesome!

I did the ballet beginners adult class and it was excellent. It's a very pleasant atmosphere and very well mirrored. Thank you Fay for the great 90 minutes that I will feel tomorrow. 🫠 See you next time 🩰🙏🏼 … || Rising Star has been such an amazing part of my dance journey! My love for ballet truly started and blossomed here, and it was one of my favorite parts of Bangkok by far. The performances were such a delight to be a part of and I’ll always cherish the lovely memories and diverse friends I made here. || Great studio, lovely teacher. Hope to come Back :) || I highly recommend Ms. Yuko's class! I love her beginner-intermediate classes, which I take every time I travel to Bangkok. 💓 … || Taking ballet lessons in Bangkok was a new experience! It was a beginner-intermediate level class with Yuko, so beginners might find it a bit challenging! The students included Japanese students, children with their mothers, and Thai students. The teacher is Japanese, but the class is taught in English. Bring water with you. If you forget, you can buy water at the playroom right in front. If I have the chance, I'd love to take another class. || If you don't speak English or Thai, it's difficult to take classes. And the teachers are incredibly unfriendly. I highly recommend not sending your child here if they don't speak English or Thai.

Friendly staff and lovely and patient teachers. My 5 yr old is very happy learning ballet here and can't wait for every class || If you want to learn ballet, you have to learn from an old institution like this.

I love this place!!!! || This is a ballet school with a warm and friendly atmosphere. The teachers are lovely and kind, and the classes are fun and stress-free. Everyone in the class is lovely. The place is well-designed, well-organized, and very beautiful. There are sofas for parents to sit and wait, and there's plenty of parking. They offer adult ballet classes. Anyone of any age can learn ballet if they're passionate about it. ❤️ If you're looking for a place to learn adult ballet, I highly recommend this place. 😊😊 || The teacher is very good. My younger sister really likes the lesson. I am considering a yoga class. The classroom is clean and easy to get to. || It's a good school, suitable for all genders and ages.

reviews_content: You will discover beautiful art spread across six floors of this museum. It is recommended to allocate at least two hours to fully enjoy your visit. The museum features intriguing paintings and sculptures created by Thai artists. After exploring, consider visiting the café.  The best way to reach the museum is by using Grab. There is also a designated area to store your belongings if needed, and they accept credit card payments. || I visited MOCA Bangkok on a weekday and had a really great experience. There was no waiting time at all, which made the visit even more enjoyable. The entrance fee was around 300 baht (if I remember correctly), and it was definitely worth it.  The collection is impressive — a wonderful mix of contemporary Thai and international artworks. I could take my time and really enjoy every piece. The museum itself is very comfortable, clean, and well-designed. There are plenty of chairs around, so if you get tired walking through the galleries, you can easily sit down and rest for a while.  There’s also a museum store where you can buy some nice merchandise and souvenirs, and a café where you can relax and enjoy a cup of coffee after exploring.  Overall, it’s a great place to spend a few quiet hours appreciating art. Highly recommended if you’re in Bangkok and love modern art! || Located a bit north from downtown Bangkok, however this is still very convenient to get to through Grab or Bolt. Apart from the evergreen art display, installations with the current exhibition GOLDEN TEARDROP are gorgeous! What's more is staffs here are super helpful to make your trip a very delightful experience :) || The museum is worth the visit and i have no idea why I kept putting it off for so long. It is a 5 floor building with a great design. The works of art are worth contemplation and it is very easy to navigate the exhibitions. There was no wait but there were other guests. There are lifts and escalators which means anybody with limited ability can enjoy the museum. Toilets are available at each floor. You get to learn about Thai artists and appreciate their artistic paths. The tickets as advertised cost 300 or 150 if discounts are applied. Payments made in cash or by card. No food or drinks are allowed as mentioned on the website. Bags are left in the deposit. The staff were kind and informative. Overall, a great visit and you will enjoy it if you would like to learn about Asian art. If you have any questions, check the museums FAQ section before coming. Ps. Some reviewers miss the point. One mentioned staff were rude and only smiling people should be employed. With that logic, perhaps Thailand should only allow tourists who are courteous, kind, polite… and obviously fast 😉. Enjoy your visit. || Experience of a life time. Such an incredible collection of Thai and international art. Felt so special to be summered in the Thai culture. Last time here was more than 10 years ago, so happy to be back again. Worth every moment. || The most beautiful museum in Bangkok. Visited on Friday and was not crowded before 2pm. It's near the immigration office (Lak Si station) so it's a perfect day trip to this area if you need a visa extension and quiet time for art. || What a marvelous museum. Nice and serene environment, well lit art work and of course the art itself. You can easily spend multiple hours here. Just go and enjoy. || One of the best surprises in Bangkok. The building itself is beautiful and full of light, and the collection gives a great overview of modern and contemporary Thai art – from huge, detailed paintings to sculptures and more experimental pieces. You can easily spend a few hours here wandering through the floors without feeling rushed or crowded.  What I really liked is how calm and well organised everything is. The spaces are quiet, air-conditioned and very well maintained, with clear signage and friendly staff. It’s a perfect break from the chaos of the city and a must-visit if you’re even slightly interested in art or design. Totally worth the trip and the ticket price. || Amazing gallery with fabulous art. Super clean and great choice of contemporary art! Impressive and must visit while in Bangkok || Amazing museum worth every penny. Can easily spend all day here, lots to see across many floors. Nice cafe too drinks are reasonably priced. We used Bolt taxi to get there, short wait finding a driver to bring us back during peak times.

Very nice place to visit. Enjoying good art in a/c room is the best.  Even on I day I went there only 2 rooms have exhibition held. || The main building is closed for renovation. They asked 240 B to see two temporary exhibits. I did not do this. They sent me across the road (walk under the bridge thru subway construction) to a gallery at Wangna Theatre (see attached photo). I am not sure this is what they intended for me to see, but it is a free gallery with mediocre art. || Only 2 of 4 halls were open when I visited. There were some of the most inspiring and creative pieces that I have seen in a long time. The work reflects my impression of Thailand... surprising, innovative, fun, and unexpected. Loved it, except I wanted more! || 7/8/25 - Almost all of the exhibition rooms/ buildings are closed for maintenance work until end of 2025. Only two exhibition rooms are available. So, please check before visiting. || Wonderful exhibition today for a single artist.  Dozens of paintings displaying  his many works and artistic styles over the years.  Standing back you would not think the same artist painted them all.  A very well done exhibition of artistic talent.  The artist is pictured here.  The rest of the museum is closed for renovations. || The National Gallery is a short walk around the corner from several other parks and museums. For only 30 Baht, visitors get access to main spaces that are open as well as the sculpture garden. Visitors should not pay anymore than 30 Baht either in advance or online. They do a lot of repairs and recirculating, so everything is not always open... With that said, we had a chance to see local artists and a Thai professor's exhibition. There is a timeline of past artists influenced by Western culture as well as a welcome from King Rama IX. Overall it's worth an hour and a half of your time. Families will love the expanse, shade and air conditioned exhibits and picnic area at the National Gallery. || Difficult to get to and underwhelming. The gallery appears to shut randomly without notice, so don’t make any special journeys in hopes of seeing it unless you call ahead to ensure it’ll be open when you arrive. The old mint and its courtyard offer a great venue to appreciate Bangkok’s 19th century, European-inspired architecture and the art therein. But not really worth the 200 baht admission. So stop in if you happen to be in the area, but don’t go out of your way. (Btw, pics allowed with no flash) || Open to the public with a 200THB admission fee.  Hosting several exhibitions including the BAB2024.. The venue is close to major other museums and sights.   Mobility assistance is offered but might need the support of staff if required to operate some lifts. Well worth a visit if art is your thing. || I can't say that this gallery is completely unworthy of the time and money spent, but I was a bit disappointed.  The painting collection is weak, and there are only four rooms open for visitors.  Across the road from this gallery, there is a National museum that is ten times more interesting and larger. And the admission fee is the same 200 thb. || The National Gallery of Bangkok 🇹🇭 Located on Chao Fa Road in Bangkok’s historic Phra Nakhon District and is housed in the building of the former Royal Thai Mint. You will see unknown and renowned Thai artworks here, both old and new.  Great place for a rainy day, that’s not a shopping mall 🛍️  Give yourself at least 1 hour here.  Ticket cost 200 baht ($6 USD) Open Wednesday – Sunday, 9am – 4pm  Directly across the street is The National Museum. Easy and convenient to see both in the same day (also 200baht ticket).

I spent about two really nice hours here. The house is beautiful, and the lush garden a calm, shady place.  I joined an English-speaking guided tour, which was easy to follow and very informative. In about 40 minutes, the guide gave us all a great overview and shared interesting background about the place.  I also had plenty of time to walk around the garden and explore a few of the other buildings on my own, both before and after the tour.  There’s a shop with lovely silk items, though many are on the expensive side. The restaurant is a nice extra and a good spot to take a break during your visit. || Jim Thompson House Museum is one of the most fascinating and rewarding cultural experiences in Bangkok. Tucked away in a surprisingly quiet and green area of the city, the museum offers a sharp contrast to the surrounding urban energy. From the moment you enter, you feel transported into a different time and atmosphere, calm, elegant, and deeply rooted in Thai culture. The traditional teak houses are beautifully preserved and thoughtfully arranged, showcasing an impressive collection of Asian art, antiques, and architectural details. Every room tells a story, not only about Thai craftsmanship and aesthetics, but also about Jim Thompson himself, his vision, his passion for art, and the mystery surrounding his life. The guided tour is highly recommended. Informative, well structured, and engaging, it adds real depth and context to what you are seeing, turning the visit into a meaningful cultural journey rather than a simple walk-through. The gardens are equally charming, lush, peaceful, and perfectly integrated into the experience, making the visit feel relaxed and immersive. Overall, the Jim Thompson House Museum is a must-visit for anyone interested in Thai history, architecture, and culture. Elegant, authentic, and thoughtfully curated, it offers a rare glimpse into a refined side of Bangkok that is both inspiring and memorable. || Quite an interesting place. TBH, I wasn’t planning on visiting the Jim Thompson House Museum; however a friend had programmed it into our itinerary. The guided tour of the house was very interesting, and the design and structure of the house (which contains pieces assembled from six other houses) was very impressive. Also the artefacts contained within were simply stunning. It appears that Jim Thompson and his incredible work to promote Thai silk worldwide left an indelible mark on Thailand. || The restaurant at The Jim Thompson House is truly exceptional — a perfect blend of elegance, Thai charm, and warm hospitality. After exploring the historic teak houses and beautiful gardens, dining here feels like the perfect continuation of the experience.  The atmosphere is refined yet relaxing, with thoughtful design touches that make the space feel both sophisticated and inviting. The food is beautifully presented, full of authentic Thai flavors, and the drinks — especially the cocktails — are outstanding.  What really elevates the experience is the service. Gam, Fon, and Arm were absolutely wonderful: friendly, attentive, and genuinely welcoming. They made the entire visit feel personal and memorable.  Whether you’re visiting the museum or simply looking for a classy spot to enjoy Thai cuisine, this restaurant is a true Bangkok gem. Highly recommended! || Spent a lovely hour and a half here. Easy to get to via the canal taxi boats. Beautiful house and lush garden. Cool on a hot afternoon. Bags go in a free locker before tour starts. Shoes on for part of tour and off for the house. We went on one of the English speaking tours. Our guide was clear and informative. It took 45 minutes in which she gave a good overview. We had time to take photos in each space. We then spent another 30+ minutes exploring the garden and a couple of buildings on our own after the tour. There is a shop with beautiful silk products, but most things a bit out of our price range! We popped into the Art Exhibition too. A lovely way to spend an afternoon. . || We thoroughly enjoyed our visit to the Jim Thompson House. Please be advised that you can enter the house only as part of a tour. English lead tours should be around every half an hour and last the same time. Our tour guide was amazing. She was very knowledgeable and witty. Not only was she able to answer any questions she also provided some memorable puns with professional delivery. 🙏🙏🙏 We also enjoyed visiting the shop and would have loved to buy more since the prices are less than half compared to European outlets. || I was surprised just how interesting the tour was - they managed to fit a lot into 45 minutes without it ever feeling rushed. The focus was equal parts Jim Thompson's life story and the history of Thai culture and architecture. Would recommend booking ahead. || The Jim Thompson House is an absolute must-visit in Bangkok — especially for anyone who loves design, architecture, or history. Every corner is visually stunning, from the beautifully preserved traditional Thai teak houses to the lush tropical gardens that surround them.  The restaurant and café are also wonderful — elegant, relaxing, and a perfect spot to unwind after touring the house. The food and drinks are excellent, with the same thoughtful design touches that make the entire experience feel special.  A true Bangkok gem that blends art, culture, and craftsmanship. Highly recommend! || Interesting man and a nice museum if you are into interiors and architecture. The arts centre next door is a very interesting design. It is quite hot, so dress appropriately. The tour is included in the entry fee and was well coordinated and interesting. || I visited the museum in 2019 and fell in love with this hidden treasure in the heart of Bangkok. I visited again to see this place again and I was still amazed at how beautiful and peaceful this place is. I would definitely recommend the visit, and I would personally go with the flow in terms of tour times. It’s a place where you can sit and relax until your tour time. It’s been 7 years since I’ve been and I’ll definitely visit again on my next trip to Bangkok.

Fantastic place to learn about the history of Bang Rak and Thailand in general. The museum consists of three beautiful houses set in a peaceful garden, each showcasing different aspects of traditional Bangkokian life in the mid-20th century.  The keepers at each house are incredibly kind and welcoming. They go out of their way to explain the background of each building and the history of the items on display.  The site features three beautifully preserved houses. One highlights the lifestyle of the original family, while others include interesting exhibits like a former medical practice and historical items from the World War II era.  Entry is free, though it is highly advisable to leave a donation to help with the maintenance and preservation of these heritage buildings. || This is a great little place to travel back in time for a moment. The house itself is beautiful and remarkably well-preserved for a home built almost 100 years ago, filled with many artifacts from the era. I especially loved the volunteer 'aunties' who went out of their way to teach us about the house and the family's history. The whole tour only took about 25 minutes and it was completely free, which is an amazing act of kindness from the family to open their home to the public. Highly recommended! || It's really worth coming here to visit, to take a look at how people lived in the early 1900s in Bangkok. It's nice to take a walk in the house and feel what it's like, and it items in the house have been maintained as they were. It's free to visit this museum and it's currently being maintained by the government. || I loved the visit to this house. Entrance is free. Quite oasi in the middle of chaos. 😅 Everything is well preserved. The descriptions are not well written and sometimes difficult to understand. I didn’t like the fact that the stuff was taking pictures and maybe video of me and other visitors without asking for permission. || It's free. It's something to do. A family home where the father was a doctor and some connection with royalty. From the World War II era through the 70s. The staff are nice. They'll take photos of you while you browse. || Staffed by volunteers, free entry. Very beautiful gardens and three houses to check out. The third one is air-conditioned, so if you need a break, that is a great place to stop.  If you like museums and enjoy seeing technology, history, architectural history, and how life used to be, it is a great place to visit.  If you are middle-aged like me, you will probably see a lot of things that are close to your childhood, from your childhood, or at least the predecessor of something you grew up with.  Really glad I walked here. || A cool museum free of charge allows you to see how Thai people used to live. There is air con in one of the buildings. Beware of the wooden stairs as they may get slippery. || You probably get a good insight of how the good old days in Bangkok was then, looking at the exhibits here. Well maintained and kept. Friendly and welcoming staff. || We had read about this museum and planned to visit but the day we chose turned out to be Chulalongkorn Day and AI was telling us it would be closed. Lucky that we ignored AI and still went there because not only was it open but it was free and lovely volunteer staff took time to show us around and explain things. Museum is made up of 3 old houses and they contain a lot of furniture, photos and household items relating to the former owners. A fascinating insight into life in Bangkok for middle - upper class people last century. || This remarkable "hidden gem" survives Bangkok rapid development, with an unassuming nature that the public mighg pass through without noticing it. The best part is that is FREE!!! There are three buildings in the yard- the resident bungalow, a clinic, and a "bachelor" house which are todays gallery with relics of the past. You will be accompanied by the staff who not only acts as guide but also to ensure the safety of the exhibits and visitors.

place_name: Kunawong House Museum บ้านพิพิธภัณฑ์ คุณาวงศ์
reviews_content: This is a beautiful art gallery museum with a wide and extensive collection of artworks. The founder of this house created it with all their heart, resulting in a truly impressive experience for visitors. There are exhibits both inside and outside the building, but the interior of the house where the owner lives is particularly fascinating and features unique pieces rarely seen elsewhere. Every space in the house is filled with the displayed art. || Very interesting museum so different from anything else I have seen. I did the non guided tour and two ladies from the staff showed me around and shared lots of details in each room, it made the visit even better. I definitely recommend this place to anyone coming to Bangkok. || Lovely tour with many historical artifacts, one of which dates back a thousand years. A fascinating insight into Thai art, culture, and history. || I discovered Kunawong House Museum through Facebook and decided to pay a visit. As a big fan of Garuda, I was really excited to learn that a large Garuda statue was on display. Seeing it up close was truly impressive & moving. The museum is exceptionally clean and well-maintained, creating a very pleasant & comfortable atmosphere. There’s also a café on the 5th floor where I enjoyed a delicious Thai tea.  Currently, they are offering a promotional entrance fee of just 299 baht, making it a very affordable experience. I highly recommend this museum to art lovers and anyone interested in unique cultural exhibitions. Access is also convenient  it’s about a 7 to 8 minute walk from Chok Chai 4 Station on the MRT Yellow Line.  One suggestion for improvement would be the addition of Japanese speaking guides, as I don’t speak English or Thai. An online guidebook is available by scanning a QR code, & it’s possible to read it in Japanese using a smartphone translation feature. However, the artworks & monuments are not displayed in the same order as shown in the guidebook, which made it a bit challenging to find specific exhibits while walking through the museum. I believe that with clearer navigation & more Japanese language support, even more Japanese visitors would enjoy this wonderful museum.  I had a great time visiting, & I truly appreciate the experience. Thank you very much! || Thank you for visiting the Kunawong House Museum. We greatly appreciate your valuable feedback and will carefully consider your suggestion to further enhance and develop our museum. || I went to Kunawong House Museum yesterday and loved it! It's a great place to see lots of Thai art and design.  The museum has many cool things to see: - Paintings by famous Thai artists - Nice furniture made by well-known designers - Pretty Buddha statues - Many other interesting items  I also liked the house itself. It looks great and uses space really well. The way the house is built makes the art look even better.  During the tour, we had a nice break for tea. They gave us delicious Thai dessert and hot tea. It was a great time to discuss with your friends and the museum owner about the arts.  If you like Thai art, design, or culture, you should visit this museum. There's something for everyone to enjoy.  I think both people who live in Bangkok and tourists will like this museum. It's a special place where you can learn about Thai culture and see beautiful art. You'll have a great time and make good memories here.  I really think you should go to Kunawong House Museum. It's a fun and interesting place to visit in Bangkok! || We would like to sincerely thank you for taking the time to share such a thoughtful and detailed review of your visit to Kunawong House Museum. We are truly delighted to hear that you enjoyed exploring the various artworks and cultural elements we have on display, and that you found our space and the atmosphere so welcoming. It is wonderful to know that our efforts to showcase the beauty of Thai art and design resonated with you, and that you had such a pleasant experience during your visit. Your kind words and recommendation mean a great deal to us, and we are honored to have been part of your journey in discovering Thai culture. We look forward to welcoming you back again in the future, and we hope to continue providing memorable experiences for you and all our visitors. || Kunawong House Museum is a hidden gem. The exhibits are wonderfully curated, and the museum's layout is thoughtfully designed, making it easy to explore and enjoy. Whether you're an art enthusiast or simply looking for an enriching experience, Kunawong Museum House is a must-visit. Highly recommended! || Quite an extraordinary place, showcasing a load of modern and contemporary Thai art in a very exquisite and tasteful setting. I'd say it's better than the MOCA. || We immensely enjoyed our tour of Kunawong House Museum. The garden sculptures and the artwork inside are all created by Thai artists and are extraordinary. Our tour was conducted in very good English by Khao Suay, and she was very knowledgeable. Highly recommended! || The Kunawong House Museum was created from a passion for art by Sermkhun Kunawong.This hous museum serves as a collection for artworks. Showcasing the evolution of Thai art from the past to the present.it feathers works that include ancient art objects and pieces demonstrating the emergence of Western-influenced techniques…. || Many thanks for your lovely review. We hope to welcome you back to Kunawong House Museum in the near future. || Unique worldwide and very interesting place. Pity that I didn't manage to attend the guided tour. Veeery nice and knowledgeable staff!

The shop owner is very kind. I ordered a portrait drawing, and the shop paid great attention to detail. He even asked me for a review about whether I wanted any additions or changes. Most importantly, they offered additional excellent services to help coordinate the packing and shipping of the picture to an international destination. || Extensive selection of paintings of all styles, genres and authors, curated and sold by a family team of very nice, welcoming people. || I recently visited Art Gallery 36 in Bangkok, and my excitement levels were off the charts! This place deserves a solid 5 out of 5 stars. What truly sets it apart is the diverse range of artworks on display – you can immerse yourself in a world of different arts, each with its unique charm and style.  Vee was incredibly friendly and helpful throughout my visit. He not only guided me through the gallery but also went the extra mile by sharing contacts easily in order to stay in touch.  Moreover, I was pleasantly surprised when Vee showed me around the entire gallery. Their passion for art was evident, and it made my visit all the more enjoyable. Art Gallery 36 in Bangkok is not just a place to appreciate art; it's a place where you can forge connections, explore diverse artistic expressions, and have a truly memorable experience. I can't recommend it enough! || Cool art gallery with lots of oil paintings. Pretty big selection in a small space, so it’s good if you don’t have too much time. || Great art, be sure to see the upstairs as that is where they keep the good stuff || Good pricing and great collection. Store owner is very friendly. || I visited the gallery today and should confess it's a such a good place to have a look at, if you're thinking to buy a painting in Thai or Lao styles and not only. Among dozens of paintings you might find even the Vincent van Gogh's Starry night! Seriously. Special thanks to Vee and Am for being hospitable! || This gallery has many kind of paintings. You can take time in art appreciation, comfy atmosphere and reasonable prices. || Good price. Large variety of quality paintings. I also like the service specially. || Pleasant and knowledgeable young art gallery owners run this very down to earth gallery and may have something that fits your bill.

First time visitors from any country should visit the Rattanakosin Exhibition Hall as a starter. Not as large as the Bangkok National museum this exhibition hall gives you a basis for thai culture. The 2 hour tour is recommended as they go through the timeline of the country, the king lineage and architectural development. Also, there are evolutions of the long boats which were interesting to me. Lots of knowledgeable facts throughout the 4 floors and a overlooking floor to see the temple on the top floor good for photos and videos. No flash however in the main building. Highly recommended! || So much fun and the staffs take very good care of us. Very impressed. Good exhibition || Truly the best ever experience to fully understand the Thai culture and history. Spent total 4 hours with a guided tour just for 100baht admission fee. Tour guide speak fluent english they even prepared a guided tour machine with super clear explanation.  If you’re interested in Thai history, cultural, Royal family. This is definitely the place to visit! Highly recommended to finish the whole 4 hours tour. The guided tour that i joined starts on 1pm sharp and 2nd tour is at 3pm. Not sure on the exact schedule. || Free entrance during certain holidays. We took route 1 that covers the history side and although it was interesting, we wish they could shorten route 1 duration and offer both route 1 & 2. English guide is available, staff is polite, clean facilities. || I took route 1 and it helped me understand the history of Thailand. It was an interesting experience and worth a visit. || Great place to learn about Thai history and culture under the influence of the current monarchy. The entry fees are absolutely fair considering the input you get by these exhibitions, made with love for details. || Excellent place to learn more about Thailand's history, culture, Thai people and also to have a great, enjoyable time. The entry fees are 70 Bhatt for the locals, 100 Bhatt for the forginers and free for any one over 60 years old. The exhibition provides a free official guide to visitors and translation. The staff are very proffisonal, friendly and helpful, providing the visitors with excllent service. || What a great experience to know about the history of Thailand and Bangkok. There are 2 routes for you to choose to learn about. It takes approximately 2 hours which is worth! If you have sometime in Bangkok, definitely check it out! || This was very very good.  There are two paths to the tour.  We took the path that has the simulated boat ride because the path with the rooms had one room under renovation. We went during the week, and since there were no other visitors at that time (hint for others), we were treated like vip guests.  The tour was great, we could take our time, we could sit in the auditorium style settings anywhere we wanted, the tour guides were quite helpful and answered our questions--even took pictures of us with the props at the exhibition hall. At the end, going to the top and looking out over the city, we had a great view of a couple temples--Golden Mount & forgot the other one, where we took pictures and rested for like another hour. Few things have been left out keeping in view the laws of govt / monarchy

Officially Thong Sanam Luang (Thai: ท้องสนามหลวง), is a 74.5 rai (119,200 m2) open field and public square in front of Wat Phra Kaew and the Grand Palace, Bangkok, Thailand. Sanam Luang is in the Phra Nakhon District, the historic center of Bangkok In the Royal Chronicle, it was written that, "In front of Wat Mahathat, Sanam Luang lies between the Royal Palace and the Front Palace. When royal cremation was held at the Phra Men Ground, the pyre set up in the centre with the Royal Palace Pavilion to the south and that of the Prince of the Front Palace to the north. The music from the Royal Palace and from the Palace to the Front would be played on opposite sides of Sanam Luang".  Sanam Luang was officially known as "Thung Phra Men" (the royal cremation ground) (Thai: ทุ่งพระเมรุ). It has been used as a site for the cremation of kings, queens, and high-ranking princes since the reign of King Rama I. In 1855, King Rama IV changed its name from "Thung Phra Men" to "Thong Sanam Luang", in common usage now shortened to "Sanam Luang".  The Fine Arts Department lists Sanam Luang as a historical site. || Sanam Luang is one of the most iconic open spaces in the heart of Bangkok. Located right next to the Grand Palace, this large green field offers a peaceful atmosphere surrounded by history, culture, and beautiful architecture.  It’s a perfect place to take a walk, relax, exercise, or simply sit and enjoy the view especially in the late afternoon when the weather cools down and the sky turns golden. You’ll see locals jogging, families spending time together, and tourists taking photos with the stunning backdrop of the Grand Palace and nearby temples.  At night, the area becomes lively yet calm, with soft lights, street food nearby, and a gentle breeze. It’s a wonderful spot to experience real Bangkok life while being surrounded by its rich heritage.  Simple, beautiful, and full of charm Sanam Luang is definitely worth a visit. || Nice place! There are the palace, the temple, the restaurants and the national museums.  They are located surrounding Sanam Luang. You can get the boat across the Chaophraya river to Wat Arun. || Must see! This palace saroundings offers a very pleasant and well-balanced experience, complemented by the exceptional atmosphere created by the surrounding temples. The environment feels calm, authentic, and culturally rich, which significantly enhances the overall impression and makes the visit truly memorable. The area is well maintained and invites appreciation of both the setting and the moment. || Beautiful and iconic place in Bangkok  Sanam Luang is a wonderful place to visit in Bangkok. The wide open space and the view of the Grand Palace and Wat Phra Kaew are absolutely beautiful, especially in the evening. It’s a great spot for walking, relaxing, and enjoying the local atmosphere.  You can see families, locals, and tourists spending time together, which makes the place feel lively yet peaceful. If you want to experience an important historical area while enjoying a calm walk, Sanam Luang is definitely worth visiting. || Amazing...early in the morning when opening is the best....and in the evening take tuktuk a go at least around and make pictures || It was a wonderful experience to attend such an event that attracted thousands of visitors from all around. Great park to relax, enjoy the greenery and exercise.  Good views of the city clean safe shaded environment for walking or jogging.  Opens early and closes late, about 10 pm.  Very accessible, close to BTS Asok or MRT Sukhumvit.  Suitable for all ages and families as well. At the end your visit you can visit the convention center to have an Air Condition dose and have a drink or meal.  The elevated walkway is really nice and great place to take pictures and see people taking pictures as well. || Benjakitti Park is one of my favourite parks—possibly my all-time favourite urban park I’ve ever visited. I first came here in 2023 and returned again in December 2025. The transformation is incredible: stepping from the crazily busy and noisy Sukhumvit streets straight into the calm of the park feels almost unreal. Birdsong replaces city noise. People are enjoying sports, walking, photography, and the many birds found throughout the park. A friendly member of the park staff even pointed me to the exact tree where the owls were living. I also met many like-minded nature lovers while photographing the stunning birds in the park. I will definitely come back whenever I’m in Bangkok. || Beautiful park! So many walking/running/bike paths. I recommend going in the morning (6-7am) or evening (5pm - later) as the weather will be in your favor (not too hot, unless you like the afternoon heat). There are some bathrooms in the park but they are not the cleanest and I would recommend bringing toilet paper and hand sanitizer. || Benchakitti Park also known as Bangkok’s "green lung" is honestly one of the most beautiful parks I’ve ever seen. It has everything. trees, a skywalk, and separate lanes for walking, running, and cycling. There are plenty of spots to exercise or just hang out. Don’t worry about the facilities either.  there are clean restrooms all around the park and tons of parking. My favorite thing to do is just lie on the grass, watch the birds, and enjoy natures . It’s relaxing with all the trees. I’d recommend going in the morning or evening when the vibe is best.  Pakin kerdniyom208 || Benchakitti Park (Suan Benjakitti) is a beautiful and spacious free-entry park located near Sukhumvit–Asok. It’s perfect for running, walking, and all kinds of exercise. The huge lake in the center gives amazing reflections of the city buildings — perfect for photography lovers.  The park has plenty of flowers, greenery, and a clean, relaxing atmosphere. The skyline views from here are stunning. It’s also very easy to access, and the parking area is large and convenient.  Overall, this park is an excellent place for a morning walk, evening run, or just to relax and enjoy nature. Highly recommended! || Very good place to relaxing exercises make love etc. well maintenance and people are very helpful friendly. Today no rain so I enjoyed well. To talk photos very good. Young and old all have places to spend time. In Sunday many people come. I did not see any restaurant but there may be. School going students come here 2025 Oct || Beautiful park. Love it very much!  Plenty of parking for the evening times. I heard that the parking can be tricky in the morning but we went around 5pm and it was fine. By the time we leave the spots open up a lot more.  The park is huge and beautiful. So many trees and very suitable for evening exercise. Many runners and walkers throughout the paths. They also popular for their long bridge that connects to other parks and other part of the city. Very cute for a date and cute little stroll. || A great park for running and other sports activities. And one can even shower at the QSNCC || This park is outstanding.  It's basically divided into 2 parts: 1.
