Having said all that, i give 4 out of 5 stars, not due to the park or staff, but due to bad actor visitors who smoke out in the open. I wish the security guards would be more proactive with smokers. I’ve seen more and more  🚬 smokers just smoking out in the open.  Today has been the third day in a row where I saw a smoker.  I think Eastern Europeans, likely Russians?  Just a guess.  It’s really annoying because by the time you can get a guard to tell them, the smoker is usually gone or have stopped.  I hope the security guards start doing more rounds and giving out more tickets and fines. Thai Parks aren’t for smoking.  I also wish the lamps were a bit brighter around the lake at night but none of This criticism of the park staff or the park itself.  The park is great.  Between lumpini, benchasiri and benjakitti, I prefer this park Benchakitti the most.  It’s the largest and most well kept.  Just hope the annoying misbehaving tourist get taken care of somehow.

place_name: Bird Watching Tower at Si Nakhon Khuean Khan Park
reviews_content: Beautiful bird watching tower. I went mid day and didn’t see a single bird but that’s not the towers fault. Primetime is usually dawn and dusk for birding.  Note: getting directions directly here from the pier/bike rental shop brought me to the wrong location in a jungle trail outside of the park (see photo). I’d recommended taking the main road into the park and following the trails and signs. || Didn’t see any birds but had a right adventure finding it (it was wrong on Google maps) which made it so much more fun. Really beautiful views and bird calls! || This tower isn't for birdwatching, but for cyclists and TikTokers taking their photos here. It's so noisy that you can't even hope to see any birds. And that's despite the fact that we were there early in the morning. If you're coming here to see birds, don't waste your time. || It's a must-see when you are staying in Bangkok and have some extra days! The perfect contrast to the busy, loud and hot city - a nice place to cool down, enjoy nature and learn something about Thai forests and animals. We finally heard some animal sounds and not only the sound of engines, honking and noise (like in the rest of Bangkok). I recommend renting a bicycle and driving around the island of Bang Kachao. Really enjoyable route - 5/5, would recommend! || Saw a snake today and spotted so many birds! I walked around the park. It’s not as big as it seems so if you’re not interested in biking then definitely recommend to go by foot. You get to see more birds if you walk quietly. The information is pretty accurate - follow the signs and you’ll find the bird watching tower easily  Mosquitoes alert!!!! I felt lucky to have wore long trousers and brought a thin jacket with me. They’ll protect you from getting mosquito bites - I’ll probably leave the place without enjoying it if I were not dressed properly || Easy to find and to climb. Not much to see without a proper binocular. And not high enough to get a view over the trees of the park. Remind that to see birds you need to came here early, around 5-6 AM. || Share a wonderful time with family strolling around the grounds and taking many pictures and videos. The park also offers many options for exercise, such as walking and running lanes, exercise equipment, and even a gym. However, the park has many ponds, which make the air very humid in the morning. The area of the park is really massive compared to urban housing around that place. So many trees grown in that park give enough shadow for the people and you can feel relax and such a relief from scorching heat of the sun when you enter that park.I really love this place. MAGNIFICENT!!!! || Perfect place to spend your afternoon after a long day at work. || Very beautiful Park in Bangkok. Very quiet given the location. reviews_content: We just finished here! My fiancée and I did the room “Last Purpose” and had so much fun. It wasn’t too difficult (while still providing a challenge!) and i feel like usually escape rooms are impossible if you don’t have a whole group — but it was totally manageable with only two people! We had a fun time — there were multiple rooms throughout the “Last Purpose” story, and lots of emotions went into it. It was an rollercoaster! We gasped, we awed, my fiancee even screamed at one point! Even better, our game maker Cue was incredible! She was intelligent, wise, and so so kind. She provided helpful hints without giving anything away, and talked with us for a bit afterwards so that we could understand the meaning behind the story (she emphasized that the Last Purpose was about family, oriented around Thai culture— we did that room because it was her favorite, and were so glad we did)!  This was such a great way to spend an afternoon in Bangkok, and it’s also in a very interesting center with a museum and café as well! Lots to do in the area, before or after the escape room. Plus, it was offered in Thai and English, so we had no problem despite the language barrier (Cue was also proficient in English, as well)! Thank you so much, Cue! Kidzooona Gateway Ekkamai — Playtime with Peace of Mind  Located on the 4th floor of Gateway Ekkamai, Kidzooona Gateway Ekkamai is a thoughtfully designed indoor playground that hits the sweet spot between fun and functionality. It’s packed with engaging equipment—from bouncy castles and ball pools to role-play stations and toddler zones—but it’s not overwhelming in size. That’s a win for parents who want their kids to explore freely while staying within eyesight.  👀 Safe & Watchable Layout The space is open and well-organized, allowing you to keep track of your child without constantly chasing them around. Whether they’re climbing foam blocks or pretending to run a sushi shop, you can relax knowing they’re always visible and within reach.  🎠 Plenty of Play Options - Active zones for jumping, sliding, and tumbling - Make-believe corners with costumes and mini shops - Toddler-friendly areas with soft shapes and sensory toys - Quiet corners for wind-down moments  🎟️ All-Day Access Once you’re in, your child can play for hours. It’s ideal for weekend outings or post-school energy releases.  👨‍👩‍👧 Family-Friendly Vibe Clean, well-maintained, and staffed by friendly attendants. Socks are required for entry, and lockers are available for your belongings.  📍 Connected directly to BTS Ekkamai via Gateway Mall, it’s easy to reach and perfect for city families looking for a safe, stimulating escape.  🧩 Zip Line Safety While Kidzooona is generally well-organized and designed for safe play, the zip line feature does raise a valid concern. Once children launch from the platform, they’re often too small or inexperienced to control their momentum. If the landing zone or path isn’t actively monitored, there’s a real risk of collision with other kids who may wander into the area.  👀 - The zip line should have dedicated staff supervision at both ends—launch and landing. - There should be clear visual boundaries or soft barriers to prevent kids from accidentally entering the zip line path. - A simple “wait zone” or traffic light system could help manage flow and reduce risk. - A single staff member stationed nearby could make all the difference. || Amazing place for kids! Recently renovated and everything feels clean, bright, and well organized. The play areas are fun, safe, and perfect for children to explore and enjoy. The staff are very well prepared, friendly, and attentive, which makes parents feel comfortable. They can also speak English, which is a big plus. Overall, a fantastic kids area and a great place for families to spend quality time. Highly recommended! || We had a fantastic time at Kidzooona in Gateway Ekkamai! It's an absolutely perfect indoor play area for young children, and a great way to spend a few hours if you're visiting Bangkok as a family.  The space is very clean, bright, and spacious, which made it feel comfortable and safe from the moment we arrived. There are tons of different play zones – from imaginative role-play stations (like grocery stores, restaurants, and clinics) to active play areas with slides, ball pits, and climbing structures.  The variety of activities is excellent and encourages creativity, social interaction, and physical movement. Our kids had a blast running around and exploring everything, and we appreciated the clear visibility from the seating areas so we could relax while watching them.  The staff was also very polite and attentive, and everything was well-maintained and organized.  If you’re traveling with kids and looking for a safe, fun, and air-conditioned indoor activity, Kidzooona is a must-visit. place_name: MELAND Siam Paragon Bangkok มีแลนด์ สยามพารากอน แบงค็อก
reviews_content: Hands down one of the best indoor playgrounds we’ve experienced! As a brand new addition to Bangkok (it just opened in early December 2025), this place feels fresh, vibrant, and packed with creative energy. It’s designed like a magical, futuristic theme park with colorful zones that blend play, education, and adventure perfectly for kids (and honestly, adults have fun too). From the moment we entered the place grabbed our attention.  The space is huge (supposedly one of the largest in Asia), clean, and well-supervised by staff. We appreciated the variety – there’s something for toddlers to older kids, and even rest areas for parents. Entry was reasonable (around 1,200 baht for kids, adults cheaper as companions), and we spent a full morning without anyone getting bored. No long waits since it’s still new, but I bet it’ll get popular fast.  If you’re in Bangkok with family, Meland is a must-visit for a rainy day or just to burn off energy. Highly recommend – 5 stars! Lots of food options out the front in the food court.  Recommend booking online tickets to avoid the queue! There is a ticket printer on the left hand side and can print out your tickets. Just book and pay online and print yourself and save the queue.  You do need anti slip socks and they sell them there fairly cheap. || The place itself is undeniably beautiful, with a soft pastel color theme that looks lovely in photos and first impressions.  However, the experience does not justify the price. The entrance fee is 720 baht per child taller than 120 cm. For a family of 2 kids and 2 parents, we paid 2,760 baht for only 3 hours.  We visited on a holiday, and the situation was extremely crowded. There were very long queues for almost every activity, insufficient staff, and poor crowd management overall. When I asked about capacity control, a staff member informed me that the maximum capacity is up to 2,000 people at the same time, which was honestly shocking for a venue marketed as a premium children’s experience.  The result is a mismatch: you pay for a premium price, but receive a much lower-quality experience than expected—overcrowded, chaotic, and far from relaxing for either children or parents.  My advice: unless crowd control and capacity management improve significantly, I would recommend avoiding this place, especially on weekends or holidays.  Picture courtesy: Siam Paragon (but imagine maximum 2,000 people in here) || This establishment offers beautiful surroundings, play equipment, and activities suitable for children over 5 years old, and also features a spacious area for children under 5. The staff provides excellent service, and the experience is well worth the price. Guests are welcome to bring their own socks, as there is no requirement to use Meland's socks. For a less crowded experience, it is recommended to arrive after 10:00 AM. || Loads of fun at the newly opened meland, some play area not fully opened when i visited however still very enjoyable 👍👍👍👍 its massive inside with many different play areas😊 … || My kids are 9 and 7.  They had an awesome time here.  We came on a Tueaday morning to avoid the crowds.  But that meant the zip line and climbing wall and cafe were closed.  None the less, the three hours sped past.  Everything here has been built with safety in mind.  So if your kids hurt themselves it is because they are kids!  Favourites - Go cart monster fight - Farm area with a cow you can milk! - cooking area - car wash - Funnel slide - train - building area  So why 3 stars?  The price.  In Melbourne there are bigger play centres with climbing walls, go carts, rides etc that charge $25 AUD with no time limit.  This was over 3000 baht for two kids.  That's over priced for 3 hours with the best activities closed.  As well, as the time progressed, the crowds came and wait times for activities got longer.  I think after a while, the novelty will wear off and the price will return to something more reasonable. || Great new indoor playground that is completely 🤯🤩there are loads of stations, rides, activities … || Came with my 3 kids and we loved it and will come again as soon as we’re back in Bangkok. It had a long queue for walk-in guests during weekdays and was overcrowded inside play areas. We have been to two other Harborlands during our one week stay in Bangkok, Harborlands welcomed grandparents for free and the experience was much happier and the service quality was much better as well.  Will not recommend Meland considering its price and overall experence. || Visited on 02/01/26 in the evening time. This place is not ready to open. Staff is not enough to operate all facilities. We were 3 adults and 2 kids. Huge place many many toys and creative places, corners or themes.  The kids loved it.  We spent sometimes 1 hour there or 2 hours maximum. But the tickets we bought we can spend 3 hours there. || The play center is spacious, but I found it somewhat underwhelming due to their policies. Firstly, they impose a time limit on play sessions, and even for older children, one adult must accompany them (while it's understandable, there are other play centers where you can safely leave your child while you go shopping). The most frustrating aspect, however, is that the accompanying adult is required to purchase a pair of socks for another 60baht, which seems like a pushy way to maximise profits.  And also masks are mandatory inside the play center, including for young children and non-participating adults. This requirement feels out of place considering we are already halfway through 2023, and it's no longer the same situation as it was in 2020.  There are a couple of massage chairs which operates for like a little over 5minutes for 20bahts.  In short, there are better and more relaxed play centers available elsewhere || It's a good concept and space, but poorly implemented, and they'll find a reason to charge you for anything... And even though we brought non-slip socks for our kids (from a trampoline park), they aren't branded with Harborland.  They require you to buy their branded socks at 60฿ per kid. There’s an open area for exercising and aerobics, and a grassy lawn where people used to lay down mats to relax and enjoy the view of the Chao Phraya River. From there, you can see two bridges: Pinklao Bridge on the left, and Rama VIII Bridge on the right.  In the past, many dinner cruises from various hotels would sail by, beautifully lit up as they turned around beneath Rama VIII Bridge. The scene at night was simply magical.  We don’t know how long it will take for that lively atmosphere to return—but what we can do now is help keep this space clean and well-preserved so it can continue to be enjoyed for years to come. || It's a great little park area where many locals and tourists come to relax. Plenty space for a picnic or exercise. Personally, it is my favourite spot to watch the sunset and boats cruising on the river. In the evening there is a chance to practise dancing with local people  and listen to the music . Can't wait to go back there. It's one of my favourite spots in Bangkok .

A wonderful weekend stop for anyone who loves butterflies. Located inside Rot Fai Park, the insectarium is well-designed with clear information boards, lush plants, and plenty of butterflies flying freely around. It’s meant to be a calm, peaceful space where you can slow down and appreciate how delicate these creatures are.  However, I did feel a bit sorry for the butterflies during my visit. Even though visitors are supposed to keep quiet, there were many kids running, shouting, and chasing the butterflies. It disturbed the atmosphere and clearly stressed the butterflies. I really hope parents help keep things calm so everyone — and the butterflies — can enjoy the space.  Aside from that, the insectarium is clean, well-maintained, and great for learning. It’s definitely worth a visit if you’re already spending time in Rot Fai Park. || We had a lovely time walking around this butterfly garden - what a wonderful thing to have in the city.  We had a walk round the park - which in itself is an amazing place and then the butterfly garden.  It is a very peaceful place, beautifully arranged with stunning planting and such beautiful butterflies and a few naughty squirrels.  A real treat and for free.  Oh and I nearly forgot - lots of interesting information and butterfly displays on the way in. || Today I visited the Bangkok Butterfly Garden and Insectarium, and it was a refreshing and peaceful experience. The garden is beautifully maintained, with a wide variety of butterflies flying freely in the large dome-shaped enclosure. Walking inside feels like stepping into a colorful, natural wonderland.  There are also informative displays about different species of butterflies and insects, making it both enjoyable and educational. The surrounding park area adds to the calm atmosphere, perfect for a relaxing stroll. It wasn’t very crowded, which made the visit even more pleasant.  Overall, it’s a lovely spot to spend an hour or two, especially for nature lovers, families, or anyone looking for a quiet break in Bangkok. 🦋✨ || We brought our students to the Butterfly Garden for a school trip. It was a Saturday but it wasn't too crowded. We want to thank Khun Jamjuree and the reception staff for being so helpful. They gave our students a talk on the Butterfly Life cycle, including life speciments to see and touch. We also got to release some butterflies! The staff were very patient and welcoming and although the park is quite small, it was well maintained and beautiful. There is no entrance fee and is open to the public Tues-Sun. We are so grateful this site is available and accessible to everyone. || Small but still a good visit there was many butterfly to see but I couldn't captures the larger ones || A love well-kept dome full of plants and plenty of butterflies. The garden around it is clearly also aimed at butterflies and different species of them are visiting the flowers there as well. Don't forget to take a walk in the park afterwards, very much worth it. || It's an okay under 30 minute experience. Quite a small area. Entrance is free you just have to register. Some really beautiful butterflies and insects. It's located inside the park so make it part of your visit. || A wonderful butterfly garden in the city. I feel it could use some extra maintaining and support, but still it's definitely worth the visit. || Had such a nice time at the Butterfly Garden. Close to Chatuchak Market so we did both the same day. The Butterfly Garden was free (have to register when you get there if foreigner) and pretty empty so you got to see everything really well and could take your time. Such a nice enclosure and could see lots of different butterflies up close. Nearby park was super lovely and an easy walk to the market. Would definitely recommend. || Nice to escape the busyness of Bangkok. Well maintained and friendly staff. We saw some huge butterflies! Free entry.

place_name: สวนชีววิถี (Growing Diversity Park)

reviews_content: This is a Wat that you will often missed walking from Siam to Central world and vice versa. My first participation on the eve of New year chanting. The feeling is awesome, everything is so well organized and orderly. Make me wanna come back again. Start of registration at 1500 and we proceed to reserve seat. Oh ya, seats are available if you are worried about sitting on the floor. During registration, donation of 60baht/pax and you will be given a chanting book in Thai though. The chanting 1900 to 0100. If you are like me who can’t read Thai, you are welcome to observe the whole chanting or leave anytime. Most people are dressed in white and please observe the dress code for temple visit. The serenity you will felt despite sandwiched in between 2 major locations for New year concert. This will definitely not the last time for me. Sadhu sadhu🙏🏻🙏🏻🙏🏻 || Beautiful temple complex.  Peaceful hidden gem among all the giant shopping malls.  Hardly anyone was there when we were there which made the visit even more special.  There is a great garden next to the complex.  Also quiet and peaceful. || Before I visit there, I read a lot of google reviews and when I arrived it was amazed me. Located in downtown but very quiet because of vast area, very close to central world. A quite place for meditation. || Like others said, it's really a nice temple nestled in the middle of the city. You can walk into the nice meditation garden here and feel relaxed and away from the city. I enjoyed being in the calmness of the temple grounds. || This little hidden temple 🛕 is a nice little spot. You can calm your nerves after a chaotic day in the city. Its also well located and definitely worth a visit. || A calm oasis hidden in the middle of the city. You are free to walk in to feel relaxed and momentarily get away from the busy streets. Beware of touts who claim to be Tourist Information outside the temple ground who will trick you that the temple is closed and offer to take you to other temple at inflated price. || It’s meant for quiet mindfulness practice or making merit, not as a tourist attraction. || Today, I had the opportunity to pay my respects to Luang Pho Phra Soem and Luang Pho Phra Sai at Wat Pathum Wanaram, Bangkok. Wat Pathum Wanaram Ratchaworawihan was built in 1857 by King Rama IV and houses three sacred Buddha images from Laos: Phra Soem, Phra Saen, and Phra Sai. Luang Pho Phra Soem was originally enshrined in Vientiane and was later moved to Wat Pathum Wanaram by royal command. || A beautiful temple located in the heart of Bangkok, known as Wat Pathum Wanaram (วัดปทุมวนาราม). I’ve visited this serene place many times to pray for good luck and enjoy its peaceful ambiance. The temple's stunning architecture and tranquil surroundings make it a perfect escape from the city's hustle and bustle. Whether you’re seeking spiritual blessings or just looking to appreciate its beauty and calm atmosphere, this temple is worth a visit. A hidden gem in the busy city that offers both cultural and spiritual experiences! || Beautiful temple situated in middle of chaos. Situated between Siam center and center world mall. Very calm place and situated near shopping area so can visit anytime. Free entry for tourist also. Best place for meditate.

place_name: ป่าชุมชนเมืองสวนป่าเกดน้อมเกล้า
reviews_content: I have a chance to visit this natural learning center & good to know that this area is forest in the city and be oxygen for people. Also Such good activity in community. I can see this forest from the airplane while i have flight from Suwannaphoom airport to south . Attractive location. || A small area for a quick walk in nature. If you are nearby it's ok to visit but don't come here especially for this. Google will not give you the correct directions to get here. You have to go by foot or bike. Navigate to the nearby temple and then go here. || Lovely family run operation.  Did a wonderful cooking demonstration and arranged for massages for our entire group in addition to an interpretative nature hike done in English by daughter who studied in Maine.  Very nice time. || It's located on Phetchahung Road, the same road as Bang Nam Phueng Floating Market, but before it. Turn right into Soi Phetchahung 16 (Soi Wat Ket). Go to the temple's parking lot and look to your left; there's a small sign indicating the way to the community forest. Follow the path. The path is narrow, but motorcycles can enter. This place is only open to groups, so please contact them in advance. Activities include fabric dyeing, composting, foot massage, making herbal compresses, and nature walks. You'll hear various bird species and see some tree species you've never seen before, such as the *Pikalangsa* tree, which can be used in many dishes. This community forest is perfect for city dwellers to breathe fresh air. || It serves as a conservation center, a learning center, and a community forest center—the largest forest area closest to Bangkok and Samut Prakan. The atmosphere is lush and shady due to the diverse range of trees that locals use in cooking and as part of community products. We invite everyone to help conserve and continue the concept of maintaining the area, preserving the unique Bang Krachao forest and its distinctive community way of life for future generations. || Nature Park in the middle of the city at Bang Krachao has a good place to relax and experience nature. || The community team and the elderly lady were the best! They truly wanted to help each other. 🥹🙏 The forest area was also very lush and abundant, perfect for activities for both children and adults. … || Great place) you can rent bicycles immediately upon arrival. There are several cafes with food and drinks || The forest park for ecotourism has many activities. Support the Pa Kaet Nom Klao community. || The weather is nice, the people are warm and friendly, the food is delicious, there are lots of trees, and there are good products to buy as souvenirs. The mango jam is very delicious.

reviews_content: Super crowded on weekends, to be honest nothing much to do here, you can feed the gulls, can take some picture or find the mudskipper and crabs.  Just a one time visit, unless you are into conservation. || A very nice mangrove and lagoon area although not well maintained. You can walk through a mangrove forest almost to the sea and around a lagoon with a a hide for birfing (this closes at 16:00 PM). There's also a canopy bridge, but you might want to wait until it's repaired.  There are lots of mudskippers, several types of egrets, storks and other types of birds. I saw a monitor too.  All in all a very nice place to explore for a couple of hours. || 1 hour hiking in sun was ok some crabs and other animals can be seen  Free parking || The Bang Pu Nature Education Center is a hidden gem for nature lovers seeking tranquility near Bangkok. Nestled along the coast, this sanctuary offers a wonderful escape from the city's hustle and bustle. The mangrove forests and wetlands here are teeming with diverse bird species, making it a paradise for birdwatchers and photographers. A must-visit for those looking to reconnect with nature just a short distance from Bangkok. || There's a beautiful walking path here that goes through the mangrove forest. It is very peaceful and quiet inside the forest. Unfortunately the path is run-down and some sections have collapsed into the sea, preventing you from walking the whole loop. It should definitely be more well maintained than this for a place so close to a popular tourist destination. || Amazing food, and one of the most beautiful sense it’s ever || Hot outside but should try with family or coworkers.some action:1. Learning abt mangroves and wild birds here 2. Planting mangroves by yourself Take care of yourself cause many mosquitoes here, bring umbrella, sunscream to protect from sunshines 40km far from bangkok Near Ancient city so you can take chance to visit(700baht/per) - worthy || Very nice nature place to get shore birds and some winter migrant birds. Free entrance. The bird hide was cooling. About 5 min walk from the entrance. || Beautiful spot to see. || Great atmosphere with nature
